items.title: AGENTS.md: choose the gate by what a change can alter, not by its breadth
items.body:
## Summary

AGENTS.md section 2 chose between `--fast` and the full gate by the breadth of a change ("large in behavior ... across subsystems"). A change touching the bridge, the attention runtime and V-offset layout read as cross-subsystem and required the full gate, whose wall time is the canonical lane's longest case (the lane already runs its cases concurrently; `--jobs` beyond the case count does not shorten it). A change inside one subsystem that could move a token needed only `--fast`, whose lanes run synthetic weights and never execute the canonical default suite.

This PR makes the gate choice follow what a change can alter:

- **Step 3** — `--fast` is the whole requirement only for a change that cannot alter a produced token or the structural audit's record and does not trigger the full gate; a timing or scheduling change that moves when a value is produced, consumed or retired can alter either; uncertainty means the canonical tier.
- **Step 4, canonical tier** — any change that can alter a token or the audit's record: `--fast` plus the canonical default suite, run to completion on the exact tree pushed; `--case` and `--smoke` are prechecks. One exception to the pre-push rule: a canonical run started on the pushed tree before push may still be running at push, recorded as pending (section 8) and completed, passing, before merge; a failure after push is a section 3 report.
- **Step 4, full gate** — a rebaseline or any change to the executable canonical verification contract. Cross-subsystem breadth alone no longer requires full. "Apply the strongest match" keeps full precedence.

Owner decisions (2026-10-02): adopt the breadth relaxation; adopt the pending-at-push exception for the canonical tier only; do not move any canonical case to nightly.

## Same-PR synchronisation

- `scripts/pre_merge_gate.sh` header: full-mode note rewritten; it now also lists the files that make up the executable canonical verification contract and what full adds over `--fast` + the canonical suite (slow serial, slow Prime Radiant, mandatory llama.cpp crosscheck).
- `scripts/hooks/pre-push` comment: no longer says "before merging a rebaseline/large change"; points at section 2 step 4 and the gate header.
- `.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md`: items 3 and 4 follow the new steps; the Canonical status section carries the per-tier completion rules and the "unmergeable until a rerun passes" consequence.
- `docs/QUICKSTART.md`: the canonical table row and the two paragraphs that described the old "large change" rule now defer to section 2 step 4; the smoke paragraph adds the named-case precheck and says why the suite's elapsed time is roughly its slowest case; the `--jobs 8` literal is removed from the edited example (the runner's default runs every selected case concurrently).

## Intentional decisions

- The sentence "Run independent long canonical jobs in parallel, not serially" is dropped: the runner's default (`--jobs 0`) runs all selected cases concurrently, so for the default suite the instruction is redundant; it was efficiency guidance, not a gate requirement.
- "canonical change" (previously undefined) is written as "any change to the executable canonical verification contract" with the file list in the gate header; a change that alters canonical *results* is the canonical tier, not full. If the old wording was meant to cover result-changing code, this is a third relaxation; recorded here rather than left implicit.
- Measured per-case durations are not recorded in docs (they move with host and pin); the docs say only that elapsed time is bounded by the slowest case.
- AGENTS.md stays under the contract test's 24,576-byte cap (24,545 after this change); the cap is not raised.

## Validation

Tree: this branch at its head. `tests/test_agent_contract.py` + `tools/doc_checks/` + `tests/test_lane_topology.py` + `tests/test_hf_report_artifacts.py` (it pins QUICKSTART/README phrases; the first CI run caught the one this PR had reworded, now restored) + `tests/test_driver_facade_surface.py` + `tests/test_bf19_pai_reference.py`: 328 passed, 55 skipped, 3 deselected — the three `test_rust_gate_selects_reviewed_benchmark_and_propagates_failures` cases fail identically on an unmodified origin/main checkout when run from a worktree without its own `.venv` (the rust lane returns before the stubbed cargo is reached), so they are environmental; they pass on a checkout with a venv. `bash -n` on the two edited shell files. No lane command, selector or pyproject text changes, so the lane-topology contract is unaffected (its tests pass above).

Reviews: the rule text went through four rounds with gpt-6-astra at thinking_mode max and three zero-context Claude reviews (plan side); the diff went through three blind rounds with gpt-6-astra at thinking_mode max (last round A0 B0 C0) and two blind zero-context Claude reviews (last round A0; its B/C items — hook text, the `--jobs 8` literal, intro wording, the post-push failure consequence — are applied in the final commit).

## Review follow-ups (after the first ready)

- Codex P1 ×3: the gate header's contract list is marked non-exhaustive and gains the `.tron` artifact modules; the canonical tier requires the opt-in cases or suite for each model, execution mode or feature path the change reaches that the default suite does not exercise (if none exists, the PR says so and gets the user's go-ahead); step 4 no longer says full contains the canonical tier — full replaces `--fast` and the default-suite run, supplemental runs still apply. The executable contract is defined by responsibility (case selection, artifact construction, orchestration, acceptance checks) with the file list in the gate header; the pending-at-push exception is scoped to canonical runs and written per required run in the PR template.
- Blind reviews of the follow-up diff: gpt-6-astra at thinking_mode max (two rounds, last A0 B0 after one wording fix) and zero-context Claude (A0; its remaining B/C: the dropped "run canonical jobs in parallel" sentence is recorded above as intentional; dependency/toolchain pin bumps are covered by "can alter a produced token" but not named in the examples — follow-up; `README.md:373` and `docs/QUICKSTART.md:806` keep a `--jobs 8` literal — pre-existing, follow-up).

## Owner decision after the first ready (2026-10-05)

The first wording of step 3 ("timing or scheduling changes can alter either; when in doubt, run the canonical tier") would have moved seven of the last two weeks' merged single-subsystem fixes from `--fast` into the canonical tier without catching anything. Step 3 now decides by whether the change can alter a produced token or the structural-audit verdict (violation count, required events) on a reachable path (from an `asim` command or the canonical runner, not test-only hooks); a timing change that reorders a value's production, consumption or retirement can; when in doubt the author asks the user and records the answer under item 4 of the PR template. Step 4 carries the same qualifiers. Reviews of this wording: gpt-6-astra at thinking_mode max two rounds (last A0 B0 C0), zero-context Claude two rounds (last A0; its B/C residuals are listed below as follow-ups).

## Known residuals (recorded, not changed here)

- A rebaseline's "supplemental runs" set is not spelled out in step 4; `docs/RTL_REBASELINE_GUIDE.md` governs rebaseline coverage and should name it when that guide is next touched.
- "(violation count, required events)" summarises the runner's structural-audit judgement; the runner also checks required-event counts and metadata and parses the report — a change that alters those without changing the verdict class should be treated as changing the verdict.
- Opt-in IR and tiny-validation cases judge more than tokens and the structural audit (IR runtime dumps, execution packages); a change that alters only those outputs is not pulled into the canonical tier by the text — intentional narrowing for now.
- The commit body keeps the canonical status it had at push; the PR template's Canonical status section carries the completion.
- AGENTS.md sits 9 bytes under the contract cap; the §7 marker descriptions are reference material that a separate cleanup PR should move to docs/ to restore headroom.

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)

- `README.md:373` and `docs/QUICKSTART.md:806` still show `--jobs 8` in command examples (pre-existing).
- Name dependency/toolchain pin bumps (numerics libraries, the Rust toolchain) among the canonical-tier examples once the byte budget allows (today 4 bytes of headroom).
- Installed hooks are copies; `scripts/install_hooks.sh` refreshes the comment text.
- `docs/canonical_results/README.md:14-15` advises choosing `--jobs` for the machine; consistent with the rule (any `--jobs` satisfies the tier), kept as is.

items.title: feat(moe_M7): Run a full OLMoE-1B-7B decoder layer on Terminus C1
items.body:
## Summary
One full OLMoE-1B-7B decoder layer, an attention prefill followed by the MoE block, with real BF16 weights, executed on the simulated Terminus C1 guest (FVP + ASIM). This builds on M6 (#9), which ran only the MoE block with HF-captured h.

- **Attention prefill in GOLD** (`layer_attention.py`):
  - q/k/v/o projections, RMSNorm and QK-norm;
  - RoPE via SAL_OP_PE, with a one-time theta-LUT load;
  - K/V copied into a KV window;
  - one SUBMIT_ATTN over 5 causal contexts;
  - o_proj and the residual, with h written straight into the MoE input.
- **V WMem offset** placed after the whole hopper-padded K region. ASIM's `attention_v_wmem_offset_chunks()` overlaps V onto K beyond 4 OLMoE tokens; that's recorded as an ASIM-side finding.
- **Builder/executor split** (`gold_builder`, `gold_executor`): templates plus binding slots, with no backend access in the builder. The M6 plan traces are pinned byte-identical.
- **1 GiB weight window** (SMS+0x10000000..+0x50000000), with ACP metadata at +0x50000000. All 64 experts are resident, so the M6 residency limit is gone.
- **TerminusSession**: PIO KV copy with readback, PE-LUT load, SVL reset. `validate_attention` requires every K/V copy to finish before attention and to land in disjoint places inside the window.
- **Host checks**:
  - HF eager capture and an attention oracle, with gates of 2^-6 on K/V and 2^-5 on the attention and layer output.
  - The HF output gate is keyed to the BF16-run selection (@tzhou-positron's #9 comment).
  - Staged weight images must match their plan spans and must not overlap.
- **C1 console**: progress lines and a model config header.

## Validation
- **C1 ("The capital of France is", 5 tokens):** layers 0, 1, 7, 12 and 15 pass; the final tree was re-run at layers 0 and 15.
  - K ≤ 3.4e-3, V ≤ 3.4e-3, h ≤ 4.4e-3, layer output vs HF ≤ 7.1e-3 (gate 2^-5).
  - Routing matches HF on every token.
  - With `--dump-rows`, 480 attention SAL rows are bit-exact.
- **Native:** all 16 layers pass; integration 32/32. A 12-token prompt (the `MAX_TOKENS` cap) passes at layer 0 with every attention stage checked.
- **CTest:** 42/42 (two tests timed out under a load average of about 110 and passed when rerun serially).

## Notes
- The paired positron-ai/asimov-os#196 moves the `moe-v1` profile and HAL to the 1 GiB window and adds `/dev/asimov-kv`. Its MoE pin bump follows this merge.
- Open for M8:
  - The 8-bit V offset limits one attention call to 12 OLMoE tokens.
  - KV rewrites after a read need an ASIM bridge payload-cache invalidation.
  - The SVL reset needs `ASIM_AP_DRIVEN_INFERENCE`.

items.title: feat(bridge): Execute programmed SAL circuit words on the guest bridge path
items.body:
## Summary

Guest MoE runtimes on Terminus C1 program SAL configuration SRAM words (the RTL RMSNorm and sigmoid helper words, plus authored Shift/Exp/Add/raw-mean NORMALIZE words for SAL routing weights). This change lets the raw SPA bridge execute those words on the modeled device path, not only the scalar-multiply word and fixed slots.

- `asim.sal.programmed_circuit`: decode (`SALCircuitConfig.from_bits`), coverage walk over the shared `sal_col.sv` leg tables, element-wise evaluation through `evaluate_column`.
- `evaluate_column`: shared leg tables (RTL default arms), mult_2 offramp, array evaluation, per-config leg resolution; PE detour and LPA offramp raise.
- `cw_dispatch`: programmed `SAL_OP_GEN` (one page) and `SAL_OP_NORM` (sum-tree DATA load in the same bundle, literal epsilon); refusals name the EXEC field.
- `spa_consumer`: EXEC lowered before its DATA load is admitted.
- `cw_fp_sqrt` (Python + `asim_rust`): wrapper NaN semantics, subnormal flush.

### Pre-existing ASIM bugs fixed
- Fixed `SAL_OP_NORM` / `SAL_OP_PE` read DATA sector 0 for sector-1 commands (`sal_fsm.sv:1979`).
- A refused EXEC left its companion DATA sector READY/owned, stalling the next valid EXEC.
- `evaluate_column` default-arm mis-selections / IndexError (list in commit).
- `cw_fp_sqrt` clamped negative/NaN input to 0 instead of the canonical NaN (`chipware_fp_sqrt_wrapper.sv:80-83,108`).
- Fixed NORM/PE silently ignored cmd_dep clamp enables (now refused).
- Stale leg table in `asim sal mux`.

## Anchored artifacts (AGENTS.md section 4)
- `tests/data/sal_known_config_golden.json`: sqrt/rsqrt rows regenerated with
  `./.venv/bin/python -c "import json,sys; sys.path[:0]=['tests','.','src']; from tests.test_sal_evaluate_column_encoding import _run_all_pin_configs,_GOLDEN_PATH; _GOLDEN_PATH.write_text(json.dumps(_run_all_pin_configs(), indent=2, sort_keys=True)+'\n')"` (format unchanged; other rows byte-identical).
- `docs/rust_hot_path_inventory.json` (on-touch, hand-maintained): open_debt `sal_programmed_circuit_eval`.
- `src/asim/sim/compute/sal_ops.py` is a pinned source of the release-cadence `tp2-short-parity-probes` publication: regenerate in the release-preparation PR.

## Performance
Scalar `evaluate_column` is 9-12% faster than the parent across `KNOWN_CONFIGS`, because each configuration's legs are now resolved once from the shared leg tables instead of per element. Programmed words are evaluated element-wise over the whole column (numpy) rather than in a Python per-element loop.

## Validation
Tested on the PR head (rebased on `7f42502dc`, no conflicts).
- Nearest tests incl. #181's bridge/Gold modules: 2523 passed, 246 skipped (environment). MoE native integration: 29/29.
- `scripts/pre_merge_gate.sh --pre-push`: all lanes pass. tests-bulk lane: 13300 passed; 2 pre-existing failures (`test_c2c_h2h_timing` ledger, Gemma tanh-gelu audit; fail identically on the parent).
- `--fast` and canonical ran on the same patch before the #181 rebase: remaining failures pre-existing (Gemma tiny-stress oracle) or environment (101 prime-radiant witnesses: Verilator not installed). Canonical (`scripts/run_canonical_rtlsim.py --jobs 4`): 8/8 cases pass with unchanged token IDs.

items.title: Attention path stats: AVX / AMX / FPGA shares and timers behind TRON_ATTN_STATS

labels.name: Skip benchmarks
labels.description: Skip benchmark jobs on the next pull request CI run

items.body:
## Short version

This PR counts how much of a model's attention work ran on each path (AVX, AMX, FPGA), and how long attention took, per layer and per pool worker (one thread of the application thread pool). 

One environment variable, `TRON_ATTN_STATS=1`, turns on the collection at run time. The numbers come out as FUSE leaves under `/model/<id>/attention/`, and as stderr summary at the end of a runtron run.

Perf impacts are neglectable. 

## Not in this PR
MoE models are not specifically scoped, it is likely MoE stats are not covered. Will add when AMX feature extends to MoE.

## Words used here

- visit: one call of `apply_page_tok`. That is one (query token, KV page of 64 tokens, KV head) triple that passed the page-level checks of `apply_page_range`. The AMX kernel serves a whole dense page per visit. The AVX loop serves the relevant K tokens of the page. An empty visit found no software work.
- forward: one model run for all users' pending token jobs. Forward class: `decode_like` when every token job has a listener (one generated token per user, but also a one-token final prompt chunk or a speculative verify step). `prompt_or_mixed` is every other forward. Under continuous batching (rinzler, the production server, adds and removes users between forwards) a forward that carries any user's prompt chunk is `prompt_or_mixed`. So `decode_like` counts pure-decode forwards only.
- listener: the consumer of one token job's logits. Every generated token has one, and so does the last token of a prompt chunk (the slice of a prompt that one forward processes). A prompt token without a listener only stores its K and V.
- pool worker: one thread of the application thread pool (`n_workers` in `summary`, 27 in the runs below). The attention workers of a forward are its last `n_attn_workers` pool workers. The first pool workers, the main helpers, do the non-attention work, and their attention rows read zero.

**Timers**, all in TSC cycles (`summary` carries `tsc_hz`):
- T1 = wall time of one model forward, taken by `forward_scope` (the one object that owns the per-forward record) inside `model::state::forward`, from just after the trace marker at its top to its return. The layers, the logits, the listener delivery and the release of the forward's synchronization latches (the latch arena) are inside. Scheduler work before and after is outside.
- T2 = busy time of one attention job on one worker. This is `attn_elapsed`, which exists today: both passes and the join, without the upstream K/V wait.
- T3 = wall time of one attention job as attention worker 0 sees it (entry to return), filed per layer. The layer and totals leaves carry the T3 and T4 keys (`wall_cycles_w0`, `period_cycles_w0` and their companions). The worker leaves do not.
- T4 = layer period on attention worker 0, filed per layer: from its first job of one attention operation to its first job of the next operation. The second minibatch of the same operation starts no period. The last layer of a forward has no period.
- T5 = `join_wait_cycles`: the time a worker spends waiting in the join with no join progress, in both join modes. In a hardware join it is the wait loop that ends when an FPGA pass or the other workers' software partials become ready. In a software-only join (CPU attention) it is the stretches of failed polls on the other workers' sections. T5 is inside T2.

## Doc and tests
Docs: `README.stats.md` describes the leaves and the switch.

Tests:

- New `t/t_attn_stats.cpp`, 17 cases. They cover tallies, rows, path sets, timers, class routing, the `forward_scope` object, the three job counts of a forward, the rows keyed by pool worker, the fold over the attention rows only, JSON leaves and their size, the leaves with the switch off, the exit report, FUSE registration with the weak_ptr rule, the last-wins takeover, and the EAGLE directory. A fork-based negative case checks that an out-of-range worker, layer or token job aborts (every hook index is a `TRON_ASSERT`). The switch rule (exactly "1") has no unit case: the reader is one function that reads the environment once, and the `TRON_ATTN_STATS=yes` runs on delphi-3bda and in the development container check the warning. The file is compiled into the `t_llama_unit` binary, so it needs no cost-data row of its own (a row needs a whole-host bench run).
- `t/t_llama_unit.cpp`: the fake-lane `apply_page_range` case asserts the stats-on tallies (32 AVX visits of 32 K tokens each, no AMX, no empty visit). The CI lane compiles without `TRON_AMX_DISPATCH`, and this case exercises the per-visit hook there. The case also reads the forward's path sets back (32 jobs `avx`, 32 jobs `none`) and checks that the visits land in the last pool row. It then repeats the call under a 2-worker split, where the same attention worker lands one row earlier. The two direct `stream_hw_joins` cases pass a real T5 accumulator and check 0. Every sweep there makes progress, so no wait is counted. After a production `apply_page_range` call, the state's own stats object is checked to follow `TRON_ATTN_STATS`.
- `t/t_amx_dispatch_dtype.cpp` asserts the amx/avx split against the kernel fakes' call counts. One section makes the fake `available()` answer false (one AVX visit that scored the whole page). After each call the path sets are read back (the AMX set exactly when the kernels ran, else the AVX set). The file also gets the `apply_page_range` argument main's copy lacks (the batch query mask). Main's copy does not compile with `-DTRON_AMX_DISPATCH=ON`, and #4557 carries the same fix.
- `t/heterogeneous_scheduler_compile.cpp`: the mixed-attention section checks the hardware join's T5 (greater than 0 and at most the join's wall time). The Q-reuse section reads T2, T3 and T4 back through `run_attention_job` (T3 includes the upstream K/V wait that a 20 ms probe makes real, T2 does not, so T3 exceeds T2). One section runs `run_joins` with no hardware plan against a producer that finishes 20 ms late, in three arms. Late producer with stats on: T5 greater than 0 and at most the wall time. Sections already done: T5 = 0. Stats flag off: T5 = 0. One section reaches `note_fpga_pass` through `prepare_hw_attention`. One case drives `model::state::forward` with the switch forced on and reads one whole record back (the class, the three job counts, T1 and the split) for a decode-like and a prompt-or-mixed forward. The fixtures that drive `apply_page_range` or `run_attention_job` with the switch on open a `forward_scope` first, as production does. This file and the direct `t_llama_unit` callers follow the `run_joins` and `stream_hw_joins` parameters.
- New `t/assertion_signal.hpp`: the fork-based helper that expects an abort, shared by `t_llama_unit.cpp`, `t_compute_attention_unit.cpp` and the negative case above (the first two had private copies).


## Why one environment variable and no CMake option

With the variable unset, a visit pays one test of a stack bool. The other hooks cost the same kind of test: three per attention job, one per failed poll and one per joined KV head in the software-only join, three per forward in `forward_scope`, and one per forward for the split. With the variable unset no hook writes memory or reads rdtsc. A visit costs est. 5,800 to 11,200 cycles (2.1 to 2.9 us per visit measured on 2026-09-01 at prompts 256 to 2048). The margin below a 1 % TPS change is therefore 60x to 400x. The A/A below is the check. 

## Off-state cost (A/A) and on-state cost

Setup: delphi-3bda, half of machine (socket 1, cards 90/93), runtron, CPU attention (`USE_HW_ATTN=0`). CPU attention is the worst case for the per-visit hooks, because every page visit is software. Model qwen-3-4b tp2, 8 users, 256 generated tokens, 3 interleaved repetitions per arm and cell. Arms: base and base2 = main 66c7bb8db1 with the variable unset (the same-binary pair gives the band). head = this branch at 9b3832eb4b with the variable unset. headon = the same binary with `TRON_ATTN_STATS=1`. TPS is the mean over the repetitions, with the sample sd. The band per cell was fixed before the runs: the largest of |base2 - base|, twice the largest per-arm sd, and 0.5 % of base.

| Cell | Arm | TPS | sd | vs base | Reading |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| prompt 1024 | base | 79.95 | 0.29 | | reference |
| prompt 1024 | base2 | 79.67 | 0.29 | -0.34 % | same binary: band 0.59 TPS (0.73 %) |
| prompt 1024 | head (switch unset) | 79.81 | 0.17 | -0.17 % | inside the band |
| prompt 1024 | headon (switch set) | 79.91 | 0.24 | -0.05 % | on-state cost: none visible |
| prompt 8192 | base | 17.12 | 0.00 | | reference |
| prompt 8192 | base2 | 17.11 | 0.02 | -0.10 % | same binary: band 0.09 TPS (the 0.5 % floor) |
| prompt 8192 | head (switch unset) | 17.25 | 0.04 | +0.77 % | faster than main, outside the band on the fast side (code placement, the same size of effect the PR 4587 measurement showed on this host) |
| prompt 8192 | headon (switch set) | 17.24 | 0.02 | +0.70 % | on-state cost: none visible |

TTFT (prefill time, max over the users), base / head / headon / base2: prompt 1024 3.146 / 3.153 / 3.161 / 3.147 s. Prompt 8192 52.65 / 52.78 / 53.01 / 52.68 s. The head with the switch set costs +0.4 % and +0.7 % of prefill time at the two prompt lengths (est. from single runs with sd 0.1 to 0.4 s: inside the run-to-run spread at 8192, at the edge at 1024).

Reading: the hooks with the variable unset cost nothing this A/A can see. The A/A resolves about 0.5 to 0.7 %. With the variable set, the counting costs nothing visible either. The pre-registered rule flips the switch to a build option only on a loss beyond the band at both cells. The environment variable stays.

Confirmation round on cbf1bb6c0c, the same cell at prompt 1024, three interleaved repetitions per arm, run after the main round on the same host:

| Arm | TPS | sd | vs base3 | Reading |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| base3 (main, variable unset) | 79.78 | 0.41 | | reference of this round |
| head2 (cbf1bb6c0c, variable unset) | 79.81 | 0.38 | +0.04 % | inside the band |
| headon2 (cbf1bb6c0c, `TRON_ATTN_STATS=1`) | 80.10 | 0.17 | +0.39 % | on-state cost: none visible |

The A/A binaries are 9b3832eb4b and cbf1bb6c0c of this branch, both of 2026-09-24. The binary comparison under Cross-checks is of 04da001cb5, on 2026-09-30.

## Cross-checks

- Binary comparison (`objdump` of two runtron binaries, main 66c7bb8db1 and this branch at 04da001cb5, `exec/attnstats-20260930-objdump/objdump-check.sh`, 2026-09-30): 384 `apply_page_range` instantiations in both. The largest instantiation grows from 11,866 to 12,708 bytes (2,055 to 2,217 instructions). Lock-prefixed instructions: 0 in both. rdtsc in `apply_page_range`: 0 in both. The largest `run_attention_job` instantiation grows from 4,281 to 4,941 bytes and from 8 to 9 rdtsc reads. The added read runs only with the switch on. All `apply_page_range` code grows by 79,633 bytes over the 384 instantiations (+6.5 %). That is the switch-on code, compiled into every instantiation.
- The exit report prints only with the switch set: 0 `[attn-stats]` lines in every run with the variable unset, and the full report in every run with `TRON_ATTN_STATS=1`.
- Counter sanity against the closed-form visit model (the 2026-09-29 run below: qwen-3-4b tp2, 8 users, prompt 1024, 255 decode forwards, 36 layers, 8 KV heads). `ready_amx_visits` = 10,278,144, which equals the sum over the 255 steps of floor((1023 + t) / 64) x 36 x 8 x 8 exactly. `pending_amx_visits` = 6,912 = 3 steps x 2,304: the three steps whose new page was full took AMX in the same forward. That closes open point 11.1 of the design page. Prefill: `ready_amx_visits` 16,515,072 and `pending_avx_full_page_visits` 1,216,512. Full pages written in the current chunk take AVX even with AMX on, because the query sees them through several mask ranges. Token jobs by path set: decode 2,016 `avx+amx` and 24 `amx`. Prefill 1,024 `avx` (the first chunk) and 7,168 `avx+amx`.
- Live reads (9b3832eb4b, 2026-09-24): while runtron ran, a poller read `summary`, `<class>_totals` and `<class>_forwards` under `<worktree>/stats/instance-2/model/<id>/attention/` every 15 s. The switch-unset run showed `"on":false` and `{}` for the totals leaves. The switch-on run showed `"on":true` and rising counts (`fuse-poll.log`).
- Kill switch (`TRON_AMX_DISABLE=1` on the same binary with the switch set, prompt 1024, one run each, 9b3832eb4b, 2026-09-24). Decode, AMX on: 10,285,056 AMX visits and 0 AVX full-page visits. Decode, kill switch: 0 AMX visits and 10,285,056 AVX full-page visits. Prefill, AMX on: 16,515,072 AMX visits and 1,216,512 AVX full-page visits. Prefill, kill switch: 0 and 17,731,584. The identity `avx_full_page (kill) == amx + avx_full_page (on)` holds in both classes. The K tokens scored in software are equal in both arms (676,823,040 decode, 1,209,139,200 prefill). The counters see the same work whichever path served it.

## What the leaves look like

Read live during a switch-on run (this branch at bff317e0d3, delphi-3bda, 2026-09-29, dev-build mount `<worktree>/stats/instance-2/model/ingested-qwen-3-4b-instruct-2507-tp2/attention/`):

```
summary
{"on":true,"model_id":"ingested-qwen-3-4b-instruct-2507-tp2","eagle":false,"amx_compiled":true,
 "amx_available":true,"n_kv_heads":8,"kv_mul":4,"head_size":128,"n_layers":36,"page_size":64,
 "n_workers":27,"active_workers":20,"tsc_hz":2699986182,"switch":"TRON_ATTN_STATS=1"}
```

The stderr summary at the end of that run (prompt 1024, 8 users, 256 tokens, CPU attention). The class label carries the rule: `decode_like/all_jobs_with_listener` is the 255 decode steps, `prompt_or_mixed/some_jobs_without_listener` is the 8 prefill forwards.

```
[attn-stats] decode_like/all_jobs_with_listener totals: {...,"ready_amx_visits":10278144,
 "ready_amx_k_tokens":657801216,"ready_avx_full_page_visits":0,...,"pending_avx_visits":580608,
 "pending_avx_k_tokens":18579456,"pending_amx_visits":6912,"pending_amx_k_tokens":442368,...,
 "attn_jobs":183600,"busy_cycles":95886519154,"wall_cycles_w0":6227932522,"wall_max_cycles_w0":3832876,
 "period_cycles_w0":8017787702,"period_count_w0":8925,...,"join_wait_cycles":2028688892,"fpga_k_tokens":0,...}
[attn-stats] decode_like/all_jobs_with_listener forwards: {"forwards":255,"wall_cycles":8610367272,
 "wall_max_cycles":48796864,"fpga_queries":0,"token_jobs":2040,"listener_jobs":2040,"kv_only_jobs":0,
 "n_attn_workers_min":20,"n_attn_workers_max":20,"token_jobs_by_path_set":{"none":0,"avx":0,"amx":24,
 "avx+amx":2016,"fpga":0,"fpga+avx":0,"fpga+amx":0,"fpga+avx+amx":0}}
[attn-stats] prompt_or_mixed/some_jobs_without_listener totals: {...,"ready_amx_visits":16515072,...,
 "pending_avx_visits":3538944,...,"pending_avx_full_page_visits":1216512,"attn_jobs":5760,
 "busy_cycles":52874188338,...,"join_wait_cycles":5367417044,...}
[attn-stats] prompt_or_mixed/some_jobs_without_listener forwards: {"forwards":8,"wall_cycles":8605423498,
 ...,"token_jobs":8192,"listener_jobs":64,"kv_only_jobs":8128,"n_attn_workers_min":20,"n_attn_workers_max":20,
 "token_jobs_by_path_set":{"none":0,"avx":1024,"amx":0,"avx+amx":7168,...}}
```

Worker leaves, read live in a repeat of the same run (snapshot at decode forward 142 of 255). The rows of the main helpers (pool workers 0 to 6) read zero. The attention rows are pool workers 7 to 26:

```
decode_like_worker_0   {"worker":0,...,"ready_amx_visits":0,...,"attn_jobs":0,"busy_cycles":0,"join_wait_cycles":0}
decode_like_worker_7   {"worker":7,...,"ready_amx_visits":348075,"ready_amx_k_tokens":22276800,...,
                        "attn_jobs":5817,"busy_cycles":2904283836,"join_wait_cycles":47550692}
decode_like_worker_26  {"worker":26,...,"ready_amx_visits":285048,...,"pending_avx_visits":45536,...,
                        "attn_jobs":5764,"busy_cycles":2840390470,"join_wait_cycles":111578888}
```

In words:

- For the decode steps: 97.3 % of the K tokens scored in software went through the AMX kernel (658 M of 677 M). The rest went through the AVX loop on the partial pending page. Every generated token used AMX, and all but 24 also used AVX.
- For prefill: 1.06 G K tokens on AMX (the ready pages of earlier chunks) and 152 M on AVX (the current chunk's own pages).
- The forward wall (T1) sums to 8.61 G cycles over the 255 decode steps, which is 12.5 ms per step at 2.7 GHz.
- The split was 20 attention workers in every forward of both classes (`n_attn_workers_min` = `n_attn_workers_max` = 20), so `active_workers` is 20.
- The software join wait (T5) is 2.03 G cycles over the 183,600 decode jobs (4.1 us per job, 2.1 % of the busy time T2). In prefill it is 5.37 G cycles over the 5,760 jobs (345 us per job, 10.2 % of T2).
- Every prefill forward carried one 128-token chunk of each of the 8 users: 1,024 token jobs with 8 listeners (the chunk-final tokens), so 8,128 of the 8,192 prefill jobs stored K and V only.

## Verification

- Unit tests on delphi-3bda (cross-avx512 preset, ingest and AMX dispatch on, fake device), this branch at 04da001cb5 (built as 8670da7f0b, a comment-only difference), 2026-09-30 00:00 UTC. Counts: `t_llama_unit` 220,158 assertions in 62 cases, `t_heterogeneous_scheduler` 2,715 in 2, `t_amx_dispatch_dtype` 1,600 in 1, `t_compute_attention_unit` 124 in 4, `t_amx_numerics` 4,109 in 4, `t_page_share_counters` 61 in 4. All pass, also with `TRON_ATTN_STATS=1`. The `TRON_ATTN_STATS=yes` run prints the one ignored-value warning.
- Unit tests in the development container (nix shell, clang 19.1.7, RelWithDebInfo, `-DTRON_AMX_DISPATCH=ON`) at 441e81178b and again at the head 8c95514924 (main 9b60b69dce merged in on 2026-09-30). Each binary ran with `TRON_ATTN_STATS` unset, `=1` and `=yes`. Counts: `t_llama_unit` 220,153 assertions in 60 cases, `t_heterogeneous_scheduler` 2,783 in 3, `t_amx_dispatch_dtype` 1,612 in 1, `t_compute_attention_unit` 124 in 4, `t_page_share_counters` 61 in 4. All pass. With `=yes` the ignored-value warning prints once per model state.
- CPU-attention runtron runs with `TRON_ATTN_STATS=1` (delphi-3bda, our half, qwen-3-4b tp2, 8 users, prompt 1024, 256 tokens, `USE_HW_ATTN=0`, this branch at bff317e0d3, two runs on 2026-09-29 at 23:24 and 23:38 UTC). Forwards 255 and 8, token jobs 2,040 (255 steps x 8 users) and 8,192 (8 chunks x 1,024), so `forward_scope` files every forward. `listener_jobs` 2,040 and 64, `kv_only_jobs` 0 and 8,128. Split 20 in every forward. T5 (software join) 2.03 G cycles in decode and 5.37 G cycles in prefill. Worker leaves 0 to 6 read zero and 7 to 26 carry the attention rows. The samples above come from these runs: the stderr summary from the first, the worker leaves from the second.

## Cost data

No new test target: the stats cases are part of `t_llama_unit`, whose row in `config/test-benchmarks.json` stays valid (the cases add about 0.1 s). A refresh of that row with `bin/slice bench --update t_llama_unit` (a whole-host run) can follow when delphi-3bda has a quiet window.

items.body:
Brings the Asimov SW Architecture Spec current with the Silver/Gold work in `asimov-sw`. Every in-review citation carries its PR number and is labeled as pending merge + Interface-Spec confirmation; nothing unmerged is stated as settled.

## What's in it
- **§9 + §2 glossary: the Silver / Gold split** (per asimov-sw [#152](https://github.com/positron-ai/asimov-sw/pull/152), in review): Silver = the command language of the abstract machine, authored/verified in Lean, no loops/branches, one-hemisphere scope; Gold = the instruction language the C1-Nano decodes; certified resolution + lowering translates 1:1. Explicit statement that production placement is unchanged (Phoenix generates, C1 executes) and that [#169](https://github.com/positron-ai/asimov-sw/pull/169)'s Silver interpreter is a host-side *verification* model, not an execution venue.
- **§9.1 authority chain updated**: executing authority today = Gold ABI v2 (`asimov-interpreter` main, pinned to asimov-sw `8808746`, v1 rejected); successor normative docs = `silver-language.md` + `gold-abi.md` with Lean modules as canonical syntax (`Cmd` = Silver, `Insn` = Gold). The Haskell model / GOLD_V1 encoding doc are no longer the stated authority.
- **§9.1 delivery vocabulary**: environment image (per-pass, no `.program` entries), `fwd_pass_plan` demoted to a private runtime materialization, out-of-band program publication (THUNK→PROGRAM magic handshake), future CBOR compiler-artifact bundle — with the **dangling `compiler-artifact-cbor.md` reference flagged**.
- **Figure 5 + §9.2 redrawn to ABI v2** (closes the v0.1.3 §16 row): 28 instructions (5 fused SPA + 23 direct), one trusted mode with admission-then-abort, erased binding classes with slot 0 unbound, depth-8 calls with legal cycles (no cycle detection), `FAIL` as the only execution fault, `runtime/moe` layer beside the interpreter.
- **§13.2 counter-model NOTE** (asimov-sw [#118](https://github.com/positron-ai/asimov-sw/pull/118), changes-requested): 19-bit internal / 16- and 32-bit published windows, N−1 predecessor thresholds with strict wrap-aware compare, CPS/SAL divergence at 2^18, C2C tx/rx asymmetry, per-counter visibility limits. Flags §13.2's current numbers as superseded-pending-merge; wholesale rewrite waits for #118.
- **§16 rows updated**: encoding shape decided (16-bit tag + statically-known variable payload); family-rename follow-up gated on the Silver stack (#113 gates; #117 approved); new row for the unfinished compiler-artifact/loader path.

## Sequencing notes
- The §9.1 command-family list keeps v0.1 names with a rename NOTE — the rewrite to the Silver `Cmd` inventory waits for #117–#125 to merge.
- No overlap with #45/#58 (§14/observability) — this PR doesn't touch §14.

items.title: Typed KV-cache tensors for packed V and native K (parent of #4424)

items.body:
## Short version

This PR addresses the maintainer's review comments at PR #4424, model code directly work on specific data layout and it makes code hard to maintain. Issue #4525 was raised to track the issue. This PR (part of #4525) adds typed views to the KV cache, instead of bare `bf16` pointers: a typed owner and view for the VNNI packed V plane, with no public pointer constructor, and a named alias for the existing row-major view of the native K plane. The alias names the layout at the kernel boundary but does not enforce it. Stored bytes, conversions, and cache behavior stay unchanged. The KV blocks now come into existence in the call that allocates their memory, with no separate construction pass.
The change passed the machine test on delphi-3bda (identical tokens in every arm, no measurable performance change).

### Not in this PR
PR #4424 (the VNNI packed-K child) is unchanged. After merging this PR, we will rebase PR #4424 and update its code to use the new tensor data type. A distinct, enforced type for the K plane comes with that PR, where K gets its VNNI packed layout. The public API in `h/libtron.hpp` is untouched.

## Words used here

| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| packed V, VNNI layout | The V plane's storage order. VNNI (Vector Neural Network Instructions) is Intel's name for the pair-interleaved operand order this layout follows. Tokens 2i and 2i+1 are interleaved value by value. One 64-byte vector load therefore holds 16 dimensions of one token pair: the even token in the low half and the odd token in the high half of each 32-bit lane. It is the B-operand layout (the right-hand matrix) of the AMX tile multiply. Address formula: `plane[(token/2)*(2*D) + 2*dim + token%2]` for D dimensions per row. |
| native K | The K plane's storage order on `main`: one row of head_size `bf16` values per token (row-major). |
| AMX, AVX-512 | Intel instruction sets. AMX is the tile matrix unit the attention kernels use for dense (fully filled) 64-token pages. AVX-512 is the 512-bit vector unit of the software path. |
| 16-lane build | `TRON_CHUNK_SIZE` is 16 (16 fp32 values per vector register, AVX-512). Since PR #4726 on `main` (merged 2026-10-01) it is the only build. The 8-lane (AVX2) build, with its row-major V, no longer exists. |
| AMX-on build, AMX-off build | Configured with `TRON_AMX_DISPATCH=ON` (the AMX kernels are compiled in) or `OFF` (they are not). CI builds AMX-on since PR #4505. Its runners have no AMX, so the kernels execute only on delphi-3bda. The AMX-off tree is a local build that checks the code compiles without the kernels. The kill switch below is a run-time setting inside an AMX-on build. |
| kill switch | `TRON_AMX_DISABLE=1`: the binary skips the AMX kernels and runs the AVX-512 software path. |
| owner, view | `v_vnni_tensor` owns one aligned V plane. `v_vnni_view` is a non-owning matrix view (rows are tokens, columns are dimensions) that holds the address formula. One element is reached through `at(token, dim)`. Whole token rows move through the bulk operations (`append_v_row`, `load_row`, `copy_token`). |
| retained slot, sliding-window slot | A KV slot is one layer's K and V storage. A retained slot keeps every token of the sequence. A sliding-window slot keeps only a recent window of tokens. |
| arena, chunk | The raw byte buffers a book allocates for its KV blocks. The accelerator cards read them directly (DMA, direct memory access). One whole-book arena holds the retained slots. Since PR #4455 on `main`, page-aligned chunks hold the sliding-window slots (PR #4456 adds the reclamation of expired chunks in the scheduler). |
| even/odd partner rule | Appending an even token also writes zeros into its odd partner's half of the pair. Appending an odd token merges into the pair and leaves the even half alone. |
| arm | One binary-plus-configuration combination under test, for example `main` with the kill switch. |
| A/B, A/A repeat | A/B: the branch binary against the `main` binary in the same configuration. A/A: the same binary and configuration run twice, as a control for run-to-run noise. |
| rc | Return code of a command; 0 means success. |

## What changes

- **`h/system/memory.hpp`**. A tag type `dma_allocation_t` (an empty type whose only job is to select an overload) and a global `void* operator new[](size_t, dma_allocation_t, std::align_val_t) noexcept` that forwards to `dma_allocate_aligned`.
  - `try_make_unique_dma_for_overwrite` now gets its memory through this `operator new[]`. Its only production caller is the KV book (`t_heap_v2` also tests it directly).
  - In C++, a call of any function named `operator new[]` implicitly creates objects in the memory it returns [N4950 (the C++23 draft standard) intro.object/13]. This covers only implicit-lifetime types, for example classes with a trivial constructor and destructor. No constructor runs, and no bytes are written.
  - Note [DMA allocation creates objects] explains the rule.
- **`h/tron/tensor/kv_cache_fwd.hpp`** (new). Forward declarations of the packed-V types, and the aliases `native_k_view<Rows, Cols>` / `const_native_k_view<Rows, Cols>` for the existing row-major `view` / `const_view` types. The aliases name the layout at the kernel signature but do not enforce it: the type is the generic row-major view, and a pointer still constructs it. The header holds no vector intrinsics. So `h/tron/kernels/amx_attn_iface.hpp` can name the typed kernel parameters and stay intrinsics-free.
- **`h/tron/tensor/v_vnni.hpp`** (new).
  - `v_vnni_tensor<Rows, Cols>`: the owner, one `bf16` array aligned to `V_PLANE_ALIGNMENT_64` bytes, trivially copyable, `as_view()` on lvalues only.
  - `v_vnni_view<T, Rows, Cols>`: the address formula, a private pointer constructor, conversion from writable to const only, bounds-checked `at(token, dim)` for one element.
  - No row type and no `expr` base. The first revision had a row expression type `v_vnni_row` and an `operator[]` that returned it. No production code used them. They were removed at the reviewer's request (review thread 4134076112, commit c12df586b6).
  - `detail::v_vnni_access`: the plane and pair-base addresses for the kernels and the bulk operations.
  - The packed operations moved here from `kv_cache.hpp` with their bodies unchanged: `append_v_row` (one token's row in, under the even/odd partner rule), `load_row` (one row out), `copy_token` (token to token).
  - Note [VNNI Packed V layout] documents the layout and the access rules.
- **`h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp`**.
  - `kv_block::v` is a `v_vnni_tensor` with the size and alignment of the array it replaces (checked by `static_assert`).
  - `kv_block::k` is a plain `bf16` array of `page_size * head_size` values. It has the same bytes, alignment and row order as the array of `bf16s` SIMD vectors it replaces (SIMD: single instruction, multiple data. One `bf16s` fills one vector register.). `k_view` now builds its views from this array with no `reinterpret_cast`. The V reads do the same since the maintainer's PR #4698 (merge commit 8e0cf77bed): `scaled_v_expr` and `fill_storage_slot` read `bf16` arrays without a cast.
  - `page::set_v` and `page::get_v` take a typed, aligned, unit-stride row (`const_v_row_view<Source, head_size, Dma>` and `v_row_view<Destination, head_size, Dma>`, the aliases from the maintainer's PR #4697, defined in `v_vnni.hpp`) instead of a pointer.
  - `page::v_packed()` returns the const packed view of one page and KV head for the kernel.
  - `book::append` copies V through `copy_token`.
  - `scaled_v_expr` (the software path's weighted sum) takes the packed view.
  - `page::v_data` and `kv_block::v_base` are removed.
  - Note [KV block lifetime]: the `kv_block` objects in an arena or chunk come into existence at the allocation call (see `h/system/memory.hpp` above). The accessors reach them through `std::launder` (the standard function that turns an address into a pointer to the object that lives there). A plain cast of the byte address would still point at the bytes, not at the `kv_block` objects. No placement new and no second pass over the arena remain. Every block type stays trivially default-constructible, trivially copyable and trivially destructible (checked by `static_assert`). The object-creation rule of the allocation call covers only such types.
  - Note [Zero-Initialized V Slots] now names the typed operations.
- **`h/tron/models/model.hpp`**. `save_v_impl` passes the V source row as a typed view whose element type and DMA flag come from the V buffer's type.
- **`h/tron/models/self_attention.hpp`, `h/tron/kernels/amx_attn_iface.hpp`, `src/tron/kernels/amx_attn.cpp`**. `qk_rowmajor_128x4` takes `const_native_k_view<64, 128>`. `weights_times_v_128x4` takes `v_vnni_view<const bf16, 64, 128>`. The kernel bodies read the plane pointers through the typed views. The tile loads are unchanged.
- **`h/tron/scheduler/full.hpp`**. The FPGA staging callback `v_head_fn` unpacks a token's V row through `get_v` into a typed destination row.

## Response to the reviewer's comments on #4424

Here are specific points raised at #4424. Sources: the maintainer's [tensor-interface review](https://github.com/positron-ai/tron/pull/4424#pullrequestreview-5270587330) and [API sketch](https://github.com/positron-ai/tron/pull/4424#issuecomment-5765866077) on #4424.

| Point | In PR #4557 | Same as suggested? |
|---|---|
| Encapsulate the VNNI representation. Too many pointers say nothing about the layout they point to. | The packed V plane is reached only through an owner and a view with no public pointer. The native K plane reaches the QK kernel as a typed view. `page::v_data` and `kv_block::v_base` are removed. |
| Follow the `tensor` / `dtensor` precedent: one interface built on `expr`, so code can convert, slice and compute on any tensor type. | Dropped by agreement. The first revision gave `v_vnni_view` an `expr` base and a row expression `v_vnni_row`, so that a host tensor could be built from a packed view. No production code read the plane that way: the AMX kernel and `scaled_v_expr` read it in place, and the page methods move whole rows. The reviewer asked why the code exists (thread 4134076112). Commit c12df586b6 removes the row and the `expr` base. `v_vnni_view` is a plain struct with `at()` and the bulk operations. |
| Introduce a `vnni_tensor` type for a VNNI-packed rank-2 tensor. | `v_vnni_tensor<Rows, Cols>` for the packed V plane. |
| Give it the usual tensor operations, in particular row-wise load and store. | `append_v_row` (row in), `load_row` (row out) and `copy_token` (token to token) keep the existing vector bodies. Single elements go through `at(token, dim)`. |
| No bare `bf16_t*` (tron's `bf16`) values without an indication of the layout. | The VNNI packed V plane crosses the cache and kernel boundaries as a typed view with no public pointer constructor. A bare pointer or the K view is a compile error (tested with `STATIC_REQUIRE`). The native K plane reaches the QK kernel through `native_k_view`, an alias of the existing row-major view that names the layout but does not enforce it. A distinct K type comes with #4424. |

Summary: four of the review's five points are addressed for the planes this PR covers. The `expr` point was dropped by agreement with the reviewer. The packed-K half of each point waits for #4424. 


## Verification


### Machine test (delphi-3bda, qwen3-4b `ingested-qwen-3-4b-instruct-2507-tp2`, `runtron --instance 2,4` on cards 90:00.0 and 93:00.0 of socket 1)

The raw tables are in the first comment on this PR.

Token identity:

- Settings: greedy decoding (temperature 0, seed 1, `--pay-for-determinism`), one user with runtron's built-in prompt of the requested length (`--prompt-length`), 256 generated tokens.
- Binary: the production code of the first commit (`85084e937c`, now `b951ba9b4c`).
- Pass rule of the plan, one comparison each: branch equals `main` with AMX on; branch equals `main` with the kill switch; branch equals `main` with FPGA attention; the branch A/A repeat equals the branch. Token for token.
- Result: all 4 comparisons are identical at both prompt lengths (1024 and 8192 tokens). The branch with the kill switch also equals the branch with AMX on (AVX-512 path against AMX kernel).

Performance A/B:

- Settings: 8 users, prompt 1024 / 2048 / 8192 tokens, 256 generated tokens, 3 interleaved repetitions, 4 arms (`main` and branch, each with and without the kill switch) = 36 runs, 0 failures.
- Pass rule, fixed before the runs: every TPS and TTFT difference of the means lies inside the band.
- Band: the larger of two values. The first is 2 x the larger arm standard deviation over the 3 repetitions. The second is the reference spread measured for this shape on 2026-09-14 (0.4 TPS, 0.15 s TTFT).

| Comparison | Result |
|---|---|
| branch against `main`, AMX on: TPS and TTFT at 3 prompt lengths | 6 of 6 inside the band |
| branch against `main`, kill switch: TPS and TTFT at 3 prompt lengths | 6 of 6 inside the band |
| largest difference | +0.72 % TPS and -0.73 % TTFT, both with the branch faster |
| per-arm standard deviation | at most 0.35 TPS and 0.23 s TTFT (each under 0.5 % of its arm's mean: 71.6 TPS at prompt 1024 with the kill switch, 53.1 s TTFT at prompt 8192 with AMX on) |

Meaning: the refactor costs nothing measurable. That is the pass rule stated above.

Instruction comparison:

- Method: 19 `noinline` wrapper functions (the moved bodies and their callers) compiled against `main` and against the branch with `t_llama_unit`'s exact clang-19 command, disassembled with `objdump -d -r`, and compared after normalisation (in-function jump and call targets replaced by a placeholder, numbered string-literal labels unified, long template names shortened, so that only the instruction sequences are compared).
- Instruction-identical: the moved bodies, that is `set_v` even/odd for bf16, float and fp16, `get_v` even/odd for float and bf16, and the `scaled_v` weighted sum.
- Differ by addressing only: the `page::set_v` / `page::get_v` wrappers that take the token index at run time (one scalar `add` fewer), and the `book::append` copy closure (same vector instructions, different scalar address arithmetic).
- Allocation path: no store through the arena pointer, no `rep stos` (the x86 block-fill instruction), no `memset` and no loop.
- One difference found and removed: a bounds assert in `detail::v_vnni_access::pair_base`, which `append_v_row`, `load_row` and `copy_token` call, sat on a frequently executed path. The second commit removed it (`TRON_ASSERT` is active in release builds).
- Scope: the wrapper comparison is of the pre-rebase code. That code still had the placement-new pass.

items.title: feat(moe_M5.3): Run the SAL-offloaded MoE layer on C1 with portable target configuration
items.body:
## Summary

Add OS support for executing a local MoE layer on simulated C1 through Terminus and ASIM. The guest runs the shared interpreter engine: SAL computes input RMSNorm and routing weights, C1 selects experts and orchestrates GOLD work.

- Add opt-in `asimov-moe-local` packaging, pinning interpreter main `f8fd5a2` (merged [interpreter #7](https://github.com/positron-ai/asimov-interpreter/pull/7)); ordinary images retain their existing interpreter pin.
- Build the runtime's `GuestTarget` (CPU, ACP FIFO core, memory windows, deadline) for the `moe-v1` profile and validate fixture windows, launch policy and simulator-default SAL slots before opening devices.
- Provide bounded, read-only ACP mappings and an isolated `moe-v1` profile derived from SAMv2, with the guest mapping probe guarding driver unbind.
- Populate private shared-memory boot backing before ASIM/FVP attach, with bounded preloads and owned-session cleanup.
- Add opt-in runtime trace points (`build_guest.sh --trace`) that report session setup and results on the AP UART.

MoE defaults off. This is functional Terminus/ASIM simulation with synthetic weights. This also restores every BridgeFwd boot (runtime, gold-v1 and moe-v1): the launcher preloads boot images into the private `/dev/shm` `ap_dram` backing (`ap_dram.create=0`) instead of `--data`, which the shared-memory `ap_dram` never received. This is the OS half of positron-ai/terminus#285. Builds on the released `fvp-v0.34.0`, `scp-v0.33.0` and `tfa-v0.23.0` pins already on main (Terminus MoE support from [Terminus #290](https://github.com/positron-ai/terminus/pull/290)). The guest bridge path executes programmed SAL circuit words from [ASIM #278](https://github.com/positron-ai/asim/pull/278).

## Validation

- Guest runner builds traced and untraced; the Buildroot package path (`BR2_PACKAGE_ASIMOV_RUNTIME_MOE_LOCAL=y`) builds `asimov-moe-local` against the pinned interpreter.
- Real C1 runs of the M5.3 runtime on the released platform stack for E=256/K=8 (`softmax`, three tokens/two slots) and E=256/K=4 (`deepseek`): all normalized, routing-weight and output lanes exact, with slot reuse and ACP mapping/binding protections.
- Ordinary (MoE off) model-free BridgeFwd boot of a fresh image reaches `asimov-runtime: ready` in 27 s.
- HAL and runtime host tests pass; OS pytest sets pass apart from device-tree checks that need host `fdtget`.

items.title: feat(bridge): Add ACP metadata delivery and FSR completion FIFOs
items.body:
## Summary

Enable C1 guest software to consume accelerator metadata from ASIM. Negotiated bridge v2 writes ACP metadata into guest memory before publishing completion pointers through the modeled FSR FIFOs.

- Add per-core COUNT, STATUS, HEAD, and POP registers using pinned RTL definitions; preserve existing v1 sessions.
- Forward the full SAL aperture for configuration SRAM and theta-LUT writes.
- Define exclusive legacy/MoE memory profiles and reject incompatible legacy preloads.
- Report ACP delivery failures through both receive paths; provide a separate qualification model for missing/duplicate completions.

## SAMv2 integration

Rebased onto main `d51fef0`. Generated SAM placement remains authoritative; ACP writes use the firmware-armed SMS bridge and share C1 backing memory. The bounded MoE profile derives weights and metadata addresses from SAM exports.

The coordinated SAMv2 OS/interpreter migration is verified in [OS #179](https://github.com/positron-ai/asimov-os/pull/179) and [interpreter #6](https://github.com/positron-ai/asimov-interpreter/pull/6). This PR does not change those repositories or the upstream ASIM/RTL pins.

## Validation

- 134 focused SAM, routing, profile and preload checks passed.
- ACP transport/FIFO and fault checks, 60 receive-path scenarios, 189 v1 codec checks, and pinned FSR/C2C regeneration passed.
- Normal and qualification model builds passed; all 11 live v1 sessions passed with Terminus's declared ASIM pin.
- Real C1 SAMv2 smoke: 38 assertions passed, covering high-address RD/GD visibility, FSR pointers and slot reuse with a synthetic v2 peer. Coordinated Linux/M5 validation now passes all nine guest cases, including slot-reuse faults; all 1,152 positive-case BF16 lanes match exactly.

The initial v1 run used the separate ASIM feature checkout and failed two SAL/SVL `build_version` reset expectations; those pass with Terminus's declared ASIM pin. This was dependency-version skew, not a Terminus forwarding failure.

### Mutation review

The scoped instrument completed: 168 mutations, 148 caught and 20 survivors matching the existing diagnostic-wording/equivalent-output registry; no timeouts or untested mutants. The nightly baseline predates SAMv2 main, so the dashboard may label these survivors unclassified; every survivor was manually checked against its registered disposition.

Related: [ASIM #262](https://github.com/positron-ai/asim/pull/262) and [interpreter #6](https://github.com/positron-ai/asimov-interpreter/pull/6).

items.body:
## Summary
This is **Milestone 5** of my MoE simulation plan. It is self-contained, and the responsibilities on the C1 are too large still... need to move the Softmax of Experts into SAL instruction set, etc. But it's a good check-in point.

Run MoE control and GOLD plan construction/execution on the simulated C1, with ASIM performing the accelerator work. Native and guest execution share one controller for routing, selected-expert FFNs, weighted combine, and bounded token scheduling; Python prepares inputs and independently verifies outputs.

- Add guest services for read-only ACP metadata, FSR completion FIFO access, progress checks, deadlines, and safe slot retirement/reuse.
- Add guest/HAL builds and isolated Terminus launching, including environment isolation, session-owned UART capture, and stale-result cleanup.
- Consolidate native/guest tests and document shared entry points, routing policies, and execution contracts.
- Align guest ACP pointers and weight preloads with SAMv2; validate the OS memory profile before launch and disable unrelated model transport.

## Integration scope

Interpreter builds and unit tests can land independently; the GOLD ABI is unchanged. Running the guest demo **requires the companion [OS/HAL #179](https://github.com/positron-ai/asimov-os/pull/179) and [Terminus #290](https://github.com/positron-ai/terminus/pull/290) changes** plus [ASIM bridge support in positron-ai/asim#262](https://github.com/positron-ai/asim/pull/262). This PR does not advance downstream repository pins.

Current execution is functional Terminus/ASIM simulation: one local layer per token, synthetic weights, E=128/256 and K<=8. It does not qualify silicon timing or Phoenix/Palladium execution.

## Validation

- SAMv2 update: 23 focused launcher/qualification checks, 11 MoE CTests, and guest/HAL/mapping-probe builds passed.
- All nine real C1 guest cases passed against the coordinated SAMv2 stack, including partial/duplicate metadata after slot reuse; all 1,152 positive-case BF16 lanes matched exactly.
- Prior qualification also covered 24 CTests and 16 native ASIM cases. Broader ASIM gate results and reproduced baseline failures remain documented in the linked ASIM PR.

items.title: feat(bridge): Add guest ACP delivery and raw execution controls
items.body:
## What / Why Enable raw bridge clients to receive accelerator metadata and completion pointers, and make configuration/progress reflect actual execution: - Add opt-in v2 ACP write/completion events with aperture, ordering and batch-capacity checks; bind fresh or adopted engines before accepting v2 and preserve default v1 framing. - Apply guest SVL Top-K and supported SAL configuration SRAM writes using the generated register map and a cited scalar circuit encoding. - Report SAL progress on physical SPM commits; drain runnable synchronous work and acknowledge standalone loads waiting for metadata or a READY-sector consumer so the client can submit the releasing work. - Reject incompatible transport/setup and cover adoption, metadata ordering, configuration boundaries, delayed visibility and queue retries; document the functional simulation boundary. **NOTE: Bridge v2 is the updated socket protocol connecting Terminus and ASIM.** The existing bridge forwarded CPU register accesses and accelerator progress signals. This extension adds the missing accelerator-to-CPU metadata path so guest C++ can consume the Top-K scores and expert IDs produced by ASIM. - **Version negotiation:** both endpoints (Terminus and ASIM) explicitly agree to enable ACP delivery. The existing v1 formats and regression vectors remain unchanged. - **Metadata writes (ACP_WRITE):** New message ID 0x22.. ASIM sends a 32-byte metadata write, its destination address and DSU ID. Terminus writes those bytes into guest memory through its modeled memory bus. - **Completion notifications (ACP_COMPLETE):** New message ID 0x23.. ASIM sends the completed metadata pointer and destination DSU/core. Terminus publishes the pointer in the guest-visible FSR completion FIFO only after the data is written. - **Guest consumption:** C++ can inspect and pop completion pointers, then read the corresponding RD/GD metadata from guest memory. - **Ordering and tracking:** completions must match prior writes, and pending state cannot carry across simulation sessions. - **Metadata drain:** ASIM finishes pending metadata processing, writes and memory responses before returning the synchronous activation reply, ensuring the guest can receive the results. - **Protocol validation:** the bridge supports the larger frames and checks versions, lengths, addresses, destinations and event ordering. The version bump applies to the simulator socket protocol; the existing hardware ABI stays unchanged. > [!IMPORTANT] > **The initial PR commit (`754a8c1f0`) completed `--pre-push` and `--fast` with baseline failures that were not introduced by this PR.** > Clean-`main` comparisons at `6b79e8ce3` show an existing stale CPS fixture, a C2C Python-version mismatch, and an existing Gemma numerical mismatch. items.title: Add ACP metadata delivery and separate command submission from simulation stepping
items.body:
## What / Why

Adds reusable ASIM building blocks for native controllers to submit work and consume completed results:

- Preserve complete routing metadata through CMN/SPM ingress and encode/decode ACP byte records.
- Deliver committed ACP bytes and completion pointers using per-core address mappings, with recoverable bounded fixture queues.
- Separate command submission from simulation stepping; retain SAL/SVL packet ownership until physical output visibility.
- Verify SAL arithmetic, routing, ordering, and overflow/retry behavior.

These interfaces support native MoE simulation. Guest execution and cache coherence remain future integration work.

**Compatibility:** ACP destinations use `acp_rd_addr` and per-core OCM/DRAM bases, independently of `spm_addr`. The legacy common-base constructor and default synchronous submission remain supported.

items.title: Add native numerical validation for Qwen3.5 MoE inference
items.body:
Add independent numerical checks for standalone Qwen3.5 MoE text inference.

## Problem

Running the full model exposed GDN buffers being overwritten before their final use, incorrect shared-gate tensor layout, and SAL scalar precision mismatches. Generated tokens alone did not establish numerical correctness.

## Solution

Preserve live GDN buffers, correct tensor loading and scalar precision, and add an independent reference with strict checkpoint comparisons for each generation step. Add a 256-expert/top-8 tiny case covering prefill and two decode steps, supported by synthetic GDN regressions and reusable validation artifacts. Mark only the three native-oracle tests whose provenance checks require the RTL checkout. The frozen tiny checkpoint digest is registered in `docs/ANCHORED_EVIDENCE.md` with its provenance in `docs/QWEN35_MOE_NATIVE_VALIDATION.md`. A review pass then consolidated the tolerance rule, margin constants, row-position derivation and comparison-JSON writes into single owners, gated capture-mode recording consistently, restored the conservative scratch reservation for undeclared GDN geometry, and made the reference refuse an undeclared head layout for grouped heads; frozen reference arithmetic and the suite's embedded checkpoint names were left unchanged.

## Testing

- On this head (rebased onto current main, RTL present): nearest and merged test files 753 passed, 0 failed; contract lane 111 passed; light gate all six lanes green (src 801 passed / 7 skipped, 12321 tests collected); tiny canonical passed (prefill plus two decode steps, tokens and all checkpoint gates); `tools.prime_radiant check` and `asim validation hf-survey reports --check` pass; the tiny fixture regenerated before and after the review fixes is byte-identical except the oracle's provenance hashes of the edited reference sources.
- The first full validation of the review pass caught a regression the light gate cannot see: a leftover function-local import in the MoE expert path raised `UnboundLocalError` whenever checkpoint capture was on (tiny canonical and four MoE external-oracle cases failed). Fixed in this head; those five cases pass again. No arithmetic changed.
- Same runtime arithmetic on the pre-rebase head 3e71b6c4: full gate red only on lanes this branch does not own (Gemma strict logits, a C2C ledger check needing Python 3.12.3, Prime Radiant witnesses needing Verilator); tiny canonical passed; two fresh real 35B runs produced ` Paris.\n` through all 40 layers with 0 mismatches against the frozen 3,574-gate suite, and their exact repeat comparison found 0 differences across 4,174 checkpoints.
- A static guard (`tests/test_import_shadowing_guard.py`) now pins that mechanism: a function-scope use of a module-level imported name must not precede a local import of it. Zero hits across `src/asim`, `tests`, `tools`, `scripts`; against the regressed file it reports both crash sites.
- The full validation restarted on the rebased head got through contract, Prime Radiant check, src and the bulk lane (bulk: only the two known non-owned failures, Gemma and the C2C Python-version check) before it was stopped to fold the guard and merge; the 35B acceptance and repeat therefore stand on the earlier head with identical runtime arithmetic (see above), not on this exact head.

items.title: Split software attention pages across cores by query (for small page and large query counts)

labels.name: Performance
labels.description: Makes things go faster

items.body:
Parallelize software attention within a page when hardware offload or sliding windows leave too few pages to keep cores busy. Workers process disjoint query ranges in both Ready and Pending phases, preserving each query's full-page reduction and section-completion accounting.

Split only single-page sections with at least 32 relevant queries, when productive page/KV-head tasks number at most half the workers. The planner accounts for worker load, speed, and setup/join overhead; it requires a 10% predicted improvement and chooses the fewest pieces within 3% of the best predicted completion time.

Measured GPT-OSS prompt throughput improves **2.38% at 2K** and **4.28% at 32K**; generation improves **1.03% at 32K**. Llama controls are equivalent to main in both phases. Changes under 1% are reported as equivalent.

| Model | Users / instances | Prompt / gen tokens | Prompt throughput | Gen throughput |
|---|---:|---|---:|---|
| GPT-OSS 120B TP4, HW attention on | 1 / 1 | 2,049 / 128 | +2.38% | equivalent |
| GPT-OSS 120B TP4, HW attention on | 1 / 1 | 32,769 / 128 | +4.28% | +1.03% |
| Llama 3.1 8B TP4, handwritten | 8 / 2 | 1,920 / 130 | equivalent | equivalent |
| Llama 3.1 8B TP2, handwritten | 8 / 4 | 1,920 / 130 | equivalent | equivalent |
| Llama 3.2 3B TP2, handwritten | 32 / 4 | 800 shared + 199 / 335 | equivalent | equivalent |
| Llama 3.1 8B TP2, generated | 8 / 4 | 1,920 / 130 | equivalent | equivalent |

Matched runs against main (`282955f1`) used Dice on andoria-cf8c: three isolated requests per context/version for GPT-OSS and at least 20 instance-iteration samples per version for Llama. Prompt counts include BOS where applicable. No throughput loss of 1% or more was measured in these comparisons.

Validation: `t_llama_unit`, `t_ranged_mask`, full build, formatting, and [CI host and FPGA tests](https://github.com/positron-ai/tron/actions/runs/35258393447/attempts/2) pass. Tests cover Ready/Pending splits, sliding windows, query coverage, completion accounting, and cases where splitting should be declined.

items.title: page_share_counters: count query tokens per KV page visit (instrumentation, default off)

labels.name: Skip benchmarks
labels.description: Skip benchmark jobs on the next pull request CI run

items.body:
This PR is the first piece of breaking up PR #3879. This PR is based on `main` and does not depend on the other breakup pieces.

## What it adds

`h/tron/kernels/page_share_counters.hpp` and five hook blocks guarded by `TRON_PAGE_SHARE_COUNTERS` in `h/tron/models/self_attention.hpp`. For every page visit - a page visit is the processing of one (KV page, kv_head) pair in the software attention loop - the hooks count the query tokens which have relevant K tokens, keep a histogram of it (slots are 1, 2, 3, 4, 5-8, 9-16, >16 query tokens) and add the per-call totals to process-wide counters. Visits without any relevant K tokens are not counted. At normal process exit, a static object's destructor prints the summary to stderr if at least one visit was counted.

The CMake option `TRON_PAGE_SHARE_COUNTERS` (top-level `CMakeLists.txt`, default OFF) adds the define of the same name to the `tron` library. Without the define the header declares no instrumentation and the preprocessor removes the five hook blocks, so a default build compiles no counter code into the library. The new test supplies the define to its own translation unit.

The CI build job leaves the option OFF, so the runtron it bundles as the benchmark artifact carries no instrumentation. The weekly coverage preset (CMakePresets.json, built by cpp-coverage.yml) sets it ON, so the hooks are compiled there and exercised by t_llama_unit.

## What does this PR serve?

Following is from example runs (qwen-3-4b, tp2 = tensor parallelism over two FPGA cards, attention on the CPU, 8 users). The numbers are workload-wide averages; they show how often several query tokens visit the same page, which is the condition under which a per-page kernel could serve several query tokens from one page load:

| Workload (8 users) | Query tokens per page visit, average |
|---|---|
| prefill-heavy: prompt 2048 tokens, 2 generated | 110.9 |
| decode-heavy, private prompts: prompt 64 tokens, 512 generated | 1.02 |
| decode with a shared system prompt: 1024 shared + 64 private prompt tokens, 256 generated | 5.06 |

The kernel in the next PR serves one query token (its four query heads) per page load. The counters tell where batching several query tokens per page load would help (prefill, shared prompts) and where it would not (private decode: 1.02 query tokens per visit).
The counter instrumentation, behind an option, makes the measurement repeatable when the batching behavior changes. A query counts as long as at least one K token on the page is relevant to it; the counters do not measure whether the page was dense (all 64 tokens visible) for that query.

## Review history

Ben [asked why the counters are global inline variables](https://github.com/positron-ai/tron/pull/3879#discussion_r3936847383) and then [named the C++17 feature himself](https://github.com/positron-ai/tron/pull/3879#discussion_r3937150401): a C++17 inline variable may be defined in every translation unit that includes the header, yet the program has exactly one object with one address, so the instrumentation needs no .cpp file.

The agent review Wade (Wado-posi) posted on #3879 ([comment](https://github.com/positron-ai/tron/pull/3879#issuecomment-5544513215)) asked for the instrumentation to leave the tree; this PR keeps it behind an option with a test and a stated purpose instead.

## Verification

Built and tested on 2026-09-08 on delphi-3bda (Intel Xeon 6962P, a Granite Rapids CPU) in a clean worktree, CMake preset cross-avx512 (with -DBUILD_INGEST_MODELS=OFF, which only skips the ingest models), once with -DTRON_PAGE_SHARE_COUNTERS=ON and once with -DTRON_PAGE_SHARE_COUNTERS=OFF (the default). 

In both configurations the two test targets and the tron library they link compiled, and Catch2 (the test framework) printed t_page_share_counters "All tests passed (61 assertions in 4 test cases)" and t_llama_unit "All tests passed (120054 assertions in 27 test cases)". In the ON build t_llama_unit printed the four [page-share] lines at exit; in the OFF build it printed none. clang-format-19 (the repository's formatter) leaves the files unchanged. 
The cost-data entry for t_page_share_counters has not yet been measured, so CI's "Check slice cost data" step fails until it is added to config/test-benchmarks.json. Update 2026-09-08: that entry is now in commit 6c735e63ae (measured on delphi-3bda with bin/slice bench --update: 0.698 / 0.700 / 0.696 s and 8 MB peak memory at the 1-, 2- and 4-slot placements).

## Labels

`Skip benchmarks`, the repository's default for every PR.

items.title: kv_cache: load last_print_bytes with a valid memory order

labels.name: Skip benchmarks
labels.description: Skip benchmark jobs on the next pull request CI run

items.body:
Two commits: the one-line fix, and a regression test for it in the existing `t_llama_unit` binary.

**The fix.** `log_kv_footprint`, the function in `h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp` that prints the throttled "KV cache footprint" log line (KV = the attention keys and values the server caches), loaded its `last_print_bytes` atomic (a counter several threads update) with `std::memory_order_release` (a memory order: the rule for how the operation is ordered against other memory operations; release is meant for stores). The C++ standard does not allow that order on a load: the precondition of `atomic<T>::load` ([atomics.types.operations]) is that the order is neither `memory_order::release` nor `memory_order::acq_rel`. The old call therefore had undefined behaviour. The loaded value only decides whether the footprint has changed enough to print the line again. The two totals in the same function (`total_bytes`, `total_books`) are already updated with relaxed operations. The load is not used to synchronise access to other data. The load therefore becomes relaxed; the store that follows keeps its release order.

Pre-existing on `main` (line 454 at a80b102c18). Ben (bgamari-positron) pointed at it while reviewing #3879 ([comment 3937077542](https://github.com/positron-ai/tron/pull/3879#discussion_r3937077542), anchored at line 487 of the head 60d66d9c04, where the same load sits inside that PR's version of the function). Separate PR so the fix does not depend on the AMX (Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions) attention change.

**The test** (first test case in `t/t_llama_unit.cpp`, a fake host test that needs no model files; placed there at the reviewer's request instead of in a binary of its own). The wrong and the right order compile to the same instructions with clang, so no check on program output can fail; the compiler, clang-tidy, ThreadSanitizer and UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer are silent too. The detector is libstdc++'s own precondition check inside `std::atomic::load`, enabled by `_GLIBCXX_ASSERTIONS` on the `t_llama_unit` target only (`add_catch_test ... DEFINES _GLIBCXX_ASSERTIONS` in `t/CMakeLists.txt`). The macro is independent of `NDEBUG` and changes no linkage names, sizes or layouts, so the checked test object links against the unchanged `libtron`. The check reaches the load because `log_kv_footprint` is always-inline (`TRON(inline)`) and is called from the constructors of the KV books (a book is one allocation of cache pages) that this translation unit already instantiates: the test file compiles its own checked copy, and a wrong order aborts (SIGABRT, the abort signal) at the first call. The new case forks a child through the file's existing `assertion_signal` helper (fork, run the callable, report the signal that killed the child, 0 for none), calls `tron::log_kv_footprint(1, 0)` there (1 byte is below the 1 GiB print granularity, so nothing is logged), and requires 0. Without the fix the case fails (`REQUIRE(... == 0)` sees 6 = SIGABRT); with the fix it passes. The case is declared first on purpose: the binary runs as one ctest test in declaration order, and with `main`'s line 13 of the 27 existing cases construct a book unisolated and abort the whole process, so the fork-isolated case reports the contract by name before that happens. The `#error` at the top of the file makes a dropped define a build failure instead of a test that can no longer fail. The bug entered `main` in 0b5bdf2c86 (2025-04-10).

Effect of the define on the 27 existing cases, measured on delphi-3bda (Xeon 6962P, one socket, mean of three runs each): all 27 pass, no other precondition check aborts, run time 6.38 s to 6.51 s (+2 %, inside the 0.26 s spread of the three baseline runs), peak RSS unchanged at 640 MiB; the control build without the define also passes. The `t_llama_unit` rows in `config/test-benchmarks.json` are left as recorded: the +0.13 s is smaller than the spread already inside the granite_rapids_6962p row (3.38 s to 3.64 s), and a refresh needs a whole-machine `bin/slice bench --update`.

Verified on delphi-3bda (Xeon 6962P, clang 19, the project's CMake preset): at this head `t_llama_unit` passes (28 cases, 120,057 assertions); the same tree with the fix reverted fails the new first case (`6 == 0`) and then aborts in the first book-constructing case with the libstdc++ message (exit code 134).

labels.name: Skip benchmarks
labels.description: Skip benchmark jobs on the next pull request CI run

items.body:
The prepare-ring-full diagnostic uses a function-static flag shared by devices whose prepare mutexes are distinct. Parallel prepares can race on that flag, and the first device to stall suppresses diagnostics from other devices.

Store `prepare_stall_reported` on `PosDevice`, protected by the existing `hw_prepare_mutex`. Each device reports its first full-ring stall independently. The flag starts false when the device is constructed; the wait loop and diagnostic contents are unchanged.

labels.name: stats
labels.description: fuse stats and tron/rinzler metrics

labels.name: Skip benchmarks
