items.title: model: one C1-SME2 (CME) per cluster (NUM_CMES=1), matching the RTL pin
items.body:
Story: [STORY-364 — Add SME2/VPU power domain support (C1-DSU)](https://www.notion.so/342d132d3cfd812bb78edd98d15249c7)

## What

The pinned RTL (`941a309cb`) builds one C1-SME2 unit (CME, Arm codename griffin) into every C1-DSU cluster — `C1_DSU_DynamIQ_Cluster_1.yaml` `NUM_CME: 1`, `griffin0_core u_cme_0` instantiated in the cluster wrapper, and the Nevis ID registers advertise SME2 unconditionally (`ID_AA64PFR1_EL1.SME=0b0010`, `ID_AA64SMFR0_EL1.SMEver=SME2`). The FVP's `NUM_CMES=0` default was therefore a silicon divergence: no SME on the model where silicon has it.

- Set `NUM_CMES=1` and the RTL-matched `DSU.cme.CMECFR` (ECC=1 from `CORE_CACHE_PROTECTION: TRUE`, CHI=0 from `NUM_COMPLEX_CHI: 1`) via `".default"` assignments on all five cluster instantiations. The per-cluster parameters stay live and init-time overridable (`-C cluster0.NUM_CMES=0` gives a CME-less A/B run).
- Keep `DSU.cme.power_on_by_default=true`: the Fast Models CME PPU registers are accepted but inert, so auto power-on stands in for the SCP's real CME-PPU dynamic-mode programming.
- Document the model limitations as **DD-12** (inert CME PPU at utility-bus `+0x280000`, unmodeled CME PPU IRQ/RAS/arbitration, partial CMECFR fidelity) and the decision as design-log **D-30**.

## FM 11.30 pitfall (why `".default"` and not the `NUM_CORES` binding pattern)

Delivering `NUM_CMES` through a top-level `PARAMETER` value binding kills every simulation at elaboration with `FATAL ERROR: An SMCU is implemented but FEAT_SME is not configured` — the binding fixes the sub-parameter out of the CADI store and the core model's internal FEAT_SME configuration never sees it. The same value applied as `-C cluster0.NUM_CMES=1`, or via `".default"` assignments (the semihosting-parameter idiom), works. Bisected against pristine main and the pinned fvp-v0.18.0; CMECFR content/escaping was ruled out. Recorded in D-30.

## Verified

- `make build` clean; `tests/run-all` **6/6** on the CME-enabled model; `cluster0..4.NUM_CMES=1` + CMECFR live in `--list-params`.
- Full asimov-os Linux boot on this model (with an SME-enabled BL31, asimov-tfa#33): userspace reached; SVE VL 128-bit, SME streaming VL 512-bit; no `sveaes/svepmull` (crypto ext fused off in RTL). `/proc/cpuinfo` from the booted system (both cores identical):

  ```
  processor       : 0
  BogoMIPS        : 2000.00
  Features        : fp asimd evtstrm crc32 atomics fphp asimdhp cpuid asimdrdm jscvt fcma lrcpc dcpop asimddp sve asimdfhm dit uscat ilrcpc flagm ssbs sb dcpodp sve2 svebitperm flagm2 frint svei8mm svebf16 i8mm bf16 dgh bti ecv afp sme smei8i32 smef16f32 smeb16f32 smef32f32 wfxt rprfm sme2 smei16i32 smebi32i32 mops hbc lrcpc3
  CPU implementer : 0x41
  CPU architecture: 8
  CPU variant     : 0x0
  CPU part        : 0xd8a
  CPU revision    : 0
  ```
- SCP firmware pytest suite: 42 passed / 16 skipped against this model.

## Consumer ordering

An SME-advertising model is only bootable behind a BL31 built with `ENABLE_SME_FOR_NS=2` (positron-ai/asimov-tfa#33): Linux writes `SMCR_EL2` at EL2 init whenever `ID_AA64PFR1_EL1.SME != 0`, and the current tfa-v0.6.0 BL31 dies silently right after its banner on this model (verified). Downstream pin bumps should take the SME-enabled asimov-tfa release before or together with the terminus release carrying this change.

https://claude.ai/code/session_01UqQuy9BCy8ER19zmCu87JP

items.title: Weight load reuse stage 03

labels.name: Performance
labels.description: Makes things go faster

labels.name: Driver
labels.description: this issue is specific to the driver code

items.body:
First pass at opening up the APIs to enable Weight load reuse with HW attention.  Currently we end up with batches of 16, and the sooner we can get gof_rodeo out of the main thread and not blockign the better.  While a gof_rodeo only happens every 4 token positions in generation, during prompt parsing we see 32 of them per batch of 128 token positions at each layer, and it's taking about the same amount of time as the Actual attention work  and should be non-blocking.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **High Risk**
> Large changes to HW attention correctness, async KV DMA ordering, and multi-device synchronization; regressions could cause wrong attention results or stale HBM reads.
> 
> **Overview**
> Expands **hardware attention** toward weight-load reuse: multi-query passes are planned with **EMEM-aware** shard/query limits (`max_shards_for_emem`, `maximum_hwattn_batch_size`), per-query `last_hw_token_pos`, and multi-Q metadata via `tok_ix_per_b` instead of a single shared `tok_ix`.
> 
> **GOF KV offload** is reworked to be less blocking on the forward path. Completed GOFs are prepared with `prep_xfer` / `xfer_n_blocks`, then submitted either **locally** or through a **per-device `gof_xfer` manager queue** (`minfifo` + batch submit under `producer_mutex`). `dma_tracker` gains `push_batch`, **`await_layer` waits all devices**, and optional `await_all` for deterministic tests. Scheduler/model changes add **multi-binding `gof_jobs`** (shared-prefix sibling GOFs), prefix-based shard eligibility, async backfill task dispatch, and barriers (`wait_for_gof_xfer_submits`, cooperative drain).
> 
> **Prompt/prefill** can stay on HW for shared K/V boundaries (scheduler no longer forces multi-query edges entirely to SW); causal tails are reconciled into SW masks. HW launch ordering in ingest moves **`prepare/launch_hw_attention` before `save_k`/`save_v`** so attention overlaps persistence. **`USE_HW_ATTN` defaults on**; bitfile **WLR** capability is checked at device init.
>

items.title: fix BS 'prompt_parsing' guard, allow batched-decode through HW path

labels.name: Tech Debt
labels.description: This label is used for things that are noticed but not connected enough to be diverted and fixed.

items.body:
## Summary

Addresses Alexey's review feedback items 5 (`model.hpp`) and 10 (`full.hpp`), about the insufficient/inaccurate 'is_prompt_processing' guard.

Replaces the forward-level `is_prompt_processing` guard that disabled hardware attention for *any* multi-token batch with per-edge HW/SW routing. The old guard (`q_batch->items.size() > 1`) conflated two unrelated things: prompt
prefill (which genuinely must run in SW) and batched decode across multiple resident users (which is fine on HW). The practical consequence was that **as soon as a second user was resident, all attention fell back to SW** — batched
decode never took the HW path.

## What changed

**Per-edge HW eligibility — `model.hpp`, `construct_hw_plan`**
- Drop the `is_prompt_processing = (items.size() > 1)` early return.
- Skip HW for a plan entry only when it actually has more than one query (`queries.size() > 1`). A HW pass carries a single causal K-boundary shared by all of its queries, so it can only serve a single-query edge. See Note [HW Attention and multi-query edges].

**Scheduler mask reconciliation — `full.hpp`**
- Replace the forward-level "if `token_jobs.size() > 1`, move all HW work to SW and clear the plan" with per-edge folding: only queries on multi-query HW plan entries (`entry.query_mask.count() > 1`) are moved HW→SW, keeping `query_mask` consistent with `construct_hw_plan`, which skips exactly those entries. `hw_plan` is no longer cleared on mixed workloads.

**Effect — batched decode now runs on HW.** Independent single-query decode queries from different sequences each land in their own HW plan entry (each a single-query edge), so they stay HW-eligible. Prefill and speculative-decode
trees (multi-query edges) continue to run in SW. Previously the presence of any second token forced the entire forward to SW; this is the behavior change the title refers to.

## Testing

- runtron with 3, 4, 6 resident users runs cleanly with these changes. 



<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes core HW/SW attention routing and join correctness paths; behavior shifts for multi-user batched decode (intended HW enablement) while prefill/speculative multi-query edges remain SW-only.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Fixes hardware attention being disabled whenever a forward had more than one token**, which wrongly treated batched decode from multiple resident users like prompt prefill and forced the whole pass to software attention.
> 
> **Per-edge HW eligibility** in `construct_hw_plan`: drops the `q_batch->items.size() > 1` early return and skips HW only when an `hw_plan_entry` has **more than one query** (`query_mask.count() > 1`)—prefill and speculative trees stay SW; independent single-query decode edges each get their own entry and remain HW-eligible. The same predicate is used at the **full edge** level (not just queries in the current minibatch) so scheduler folding and plan construction stay aligned when edges split across minibatches.
> 
> **Scheduler reconciliation** in `full.hpp`: instead of moving all HW work to SW and clearing `hw_plan` when `token_jobs.size() > 1`, it folds **only** queries on multi-query HW plan entries from HW→SW, with partial range updates when a range mixes prompt and decode queries. `hw_plan` is retained for mixed workloads.
> 
> **Attention join hardening** in `self_attention.hpp`: when merging HW pass results, **skip passes that do not include the current batch job** so unpack/join does not read never-DMA'd buffers; SW scratchpads are marked valid only when `m_star` has left `-inf`, reducing bad joins under multi-token batches with multiple users (symptom gate, with a TODO on root cause).
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 4f5c3da03f46e18d791b7f147d123e1b8f8a04d6. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>
<!-- /CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

items.title: Cache cpu_frequency_hz reciprocals for cycles_to_ns / ns_to_cycles

labels.name: Performance
labels.description: Makes things go faster

items.body:
## Summary
- Replace the two 64-bit divides in `precise_scale` with a 64x64→128 multiply + shift (one `mulq` on x86_64) — `cycles_to_ns` / `ns_to_cycles` drop from ~30–50 cycles to ~5.
- The TSC calibration thread caches fixed-point reciprocals of `cpu_frequency_hz` alongside it and refreshes them on every freq update; writes are ordered reciprocal-then-frequency so a reader past the existing `!= 0` gate observes a valid pair.
- `ns_per_cycle` stored in Q.64 (all fractional — ns-per-cycle < 1 for any freq > 1 GHz). `cycles_per_ns` stored in Q.61, reserving 3 integer bits for the small cycles-per-ns rate (covers up to ~8 GHz; realistic x86_64 invariant TSC is 2–4 GHz). Round-to-nearest at both reciprocal computation and the final shift preserves the strict round-trip behavior the existing precision tests rely on.

## Test plan
- [x] `make t_system` — all 12 cases pass, including the strict round-trip at `ns = 1e10` and the precision sweep from 1 µs to `cycles_to_ns(UINT64_MAX - 1000)` (error is 0 ns for all realistic scales, 1 ns at the UINT64_MAX edge vs. the 1000 ns tolerance).
- [x] `make t_mwaitx` — passes (heavy `ns_to_cycles` user).
- [x] `make lint`.
- [ ] Confirm on a non-AMD host (Intel Xeon) that calibration converges and conversions stay accurate.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Touches core timestamp math used widely via get_corrected_ns; ordering and rounding must stay correct, though tests and asserts mitigate regressions.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Speeds up hot-path TSC conversions** by caching `cpu_frequency_hz` reciprocals as Q3.61 fixed-point values and using `__uint128_t` multiply + round-shift in `cycles_to_ns` / `ns_to_cycles` instead of `precise_scale`’s 64-bit divides.
> 
> The TSC calibration thread recomputes those reciprocals on every frequency update via new `update_freq_reciprocals()` (with freq bounds asserts) and publishes them **before** writing `cpu_frequency_hz`, so readers past the existing `cpu_frequency_hz != 0` gate always see a consistent pair. Header documentation in **Note [Cycle Frequency Reciprocals]** explains the format and ordering; `precise_scale` is left in place for other callers (e.g. in-loop `new_freq` estimation).
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 34d87818658dfff8580eb63b42e678557af96bcf. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>

items.title: Free and repopulate GOF staging buffers after DMA completion (Story 2814)

labels.name: Continuous integration
labels.description: Relates to CI

items.body:
Treat each gof's two 8 KB hwcacheblock staging buffers (k.data/v.data) as a reconstructable cache: free them once every in-flight DMA that reads them has completed, and rebuild on demand (reacquire + rebuild position tables + repopulate from the host KV pages) when a later submission needs the GOF. The durable copies remain the host books and device HBM, so the free is a cache eviction -- GOF identity (gal.gofs[layer], gof_job refs, shard state) is unchanged. See Note [GOF staging eviction].

Interface / behavior:
- gof: add dma_inflight (atomic) + staging_mutex, prepare_for_dma() (reacquire + populate + reserve a credit under the mutex before xfer_gof), free_staging_if_idle() (frees both buffers once dma_inflight hits 0), and the inflight_guard RAII credit (commit() after xfer_gof keeps it).
- hwcacheblock: alloc_buffer/release_buffer/clear/is_allocated; k/v gain non-virtual rebuild_positions()/reacquire_buffer() (no new pos virtuals).
- pending_xfer: add pinned_gof (shared_ptr<gof>) pinning staging for the life of its in-flight DMA and serving as the dma_inflight decrement target.
- dma_tracker::push() is now noexcept (a post-submit failure terminates rather than unwinding into a free-under-DMA); poll_completions decrements and frees outside dma_tracker::mu to avoid a staging_mutex<->mu lock-order inversion.
- Submission sites gof_rodeo_impl and backfill_shard route through prepare_for_dma / commit / push.

Tests:
- t_dma_tracker (pos_fake): staging lifecycle, inflight_guard, poll-frees-after- last, clear-drops-pin, prepare/free allocation-neutrality.
- t_gof_dma (FPGA): free -> reacquire -> fill -> xfer -> readback; and prepare_for_dma reacquire/populate/credit.
- t_gof_staging_leaks (FPGA, new): real DMA-heap allocation-balance leak suite across submit/track/complete/free + multi-device fanout.

Validated: make build-test clean; t_dma_tracker 33/1718; t_gof_dma and t_gof_staging_leaks pass on FPGA (slice-scoped); make format + lint clean.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **High Risk**
> Changes concurrent DMA submission, completion, and host buffer lifetime for hardware KV offload; races or premature free could corrupt in-flight transfers or leak staging memory.
> 
> **Overview**
> **GOF host staging is now evictable** after DMA lands in HBM: each `gof`'s two 8 KB `hwcacheblock` buffers are treated as a cache over the durable host KV pages and device copy, not permanent allocations.
> 
> `hwcacheblock` gains explicit **alloc/release/reacquire** and **`build_indexes()`** so K/V pointer tables stay valid when staging is freed and reallocated. `gof` adds **`dma_inflight`**, a **`staging_busy` CAS gate**, **`prepare_for_dma()`** (reacquire, populate, reserve credit), **`free_staging_if_idle()`**, and **`inflight_guard`** (rollback unless **`commit()`** after `xfer_gof`).
> 
> **`dma_tracker`** records **`pinned_gof`** on each `pending_xfer`, makes **`push()` noexcept**, and **`poll_completions()`** decrements credits and calls **`free_staging_if_idle()` outside the tracker mutex**. **`gof_rodeo_impl`** and **`backfill_shard`** use the prepare/commit/push path and hold **`shared_ptr<gof>`** through submit.
> 
> Tests cover fake and FPGA paths, including new **`t_gof_staging_leaks`** for DMA-heap balance and tracker lifecycle.
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 678f559d5d9dc77bbcd69ca27a39f2d698ef6528. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>

items.title: Move inwork queue from CKSTAILQ to new minfifo implementation

labels.name: Type: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: Performance
labels.description: Makes things go faster

labels.name: Driver
labels.description: this issue is specific to the driver code

items.body:
Add minfifo, a minimal Vyukov style Multi Producer Single Consumer Fifo queue and move from  using the CKSTAILQ to it for enqueueiung to devices

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes the hot path between app threads and TX workers; correctness depends on minfifo memory ordering and queue-full handling, though new tests cover MPSC behavior.
> 
> **Overview**
> Replaces the per-device **in-work** path from a **mutex-protected Concurrency Kit STAILQ** to a new **`tron::minfifo`** lock-free **multi-producer / single-consumer** ring (2048 slots via `inwork_ring_size`).
> 
> **Enqueue** (`enqueue_hardware_matmul_job_to_device`) no longer takes `inwork_mutex`; it atomically updates `enqueued_work` / `work_req_count` and pushes `wqentry*` into `inwork_queue`, **asserting** on overflow instead of an unbounded list.
> 
> The **TX worker** dequeues with `dequeue()` and blocks on **`mwaitx`** using `dequeue_wait_hint()` on the next cell’s sequence word, rather than watching the STAILQ head pointer.
>

items.title: Free and repopulate GOF staging buffers after DMA completion (Story 2814)

labels.name: Continuous integration
labels.description: Relates to CI

items.body:
Treat each gof's two 8 KB hwcacheblock staging buffers (k.data/v.data) as a reconstructable cache: free them once every in-flight DMA that reads them has completed, and rebuild on demand (reacquire + rebuild position tables + repopulate from the host KV pages) when a later submission needs the GOF. The durable copies remain the host books and device HBM, so the free is a cache eviction -- GOF identity (gal.gofs[layer], gof_job refs, shard state) is unchanged. See Note [GOF staging eviction].

Interface / behavior:
- gof: add dma_inflight (atomic) + staging_mutex, prepare_for_dma() (reacquire + populate + reserve a credit under the mutex before xfer_gof), free_staging_if_idle() (frees both buffers once dma_inflight hits 0), and the inflight_guard RAII credit (commit() after xfer_gof keeps it).
- hwcacheblock: alloc_buffer/release_buffer/clear/is_allocated; k/v gain non-virtual rebuild_positions()/reacquire_buffer() (no new pos virtuals).
- pending_xfer: add pinned_gof (shared_ptr<gof>) pinning staging for the life of its in-flight DMA and serving as the dma_inflight decrement target.
- dma_tracker::push() is now noexcept (a post-submit failure terminates rather than unwinding into a free-under-DMA); poll_completions decrements and frees outside dma_tracker::mu to avoid a staging_mutex<->mu lock-order inversion.
- Submission sites gof_rodeo_impl and backfill_shard route through prepare_for_dma / commit / push.

Tests:
- t_dma_tracker (pos_fake): staging lifecycle, inflight_guard, poll-frees-after- last, clear-drops-pin, prepare/free allocation-neutrality.
- t_gof_dma (FPGA): free -> reacquire -> fill -> xfer -> readback; and prepare_for_dma reacquire/populate/credit.
- t_gof_staging_leaks (FPGA, new): real DMA-heap allocation-balance leak suite across submit/track/complete/free + multi-device fanout.

Validated: make build-test clean; t_dma_tracker 33/1718; t_gof_dma and t_gof_staging_leaks pass on FPGA (slice-scoped); make format + lint clean.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **High Risk**
> Changes DMA staging lifetime, concurrent free vs submit paths, and lock ordering; bugs could use-after-free staging under live DMA or corrupt GOF state.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Story 2814** treats each GOF’s two 8 KB `hwcacheblock` staging buffers as a **reconstructable cache**: after HBM DMA completes, `dma_tracker::poll_completions` can evict them via `gof::free_staging_if_idle`; the next transfer uses `prepare_for_dma` to reallocate, rebuild `positions` tables, and repopulate from host KV pages.
> 
> The lifecycle is guarded by **`dma_inflight`**, **`staging_mutex`**, and **`inflight_guard`**: credit is reserved before `xfer_gof`, **`commit()`** after descriptors are live, and **`pending_xfer::pinned_gof`** keeps the GOF (and staging) alive until completion decrements the last credit. **`dma_tracker::push` is `noexcept`** so post-submit failures terminate instead of freeing staging under active DMA; staging frees run **outside** the tracker mutex to avoid lock inversion with `staging_mutex`.
> 
> **`gof_rodeo_impl`** and **`backfill_shard`** share this path. **`clear()`** remains an abandon-only shutdown hook and does not treat queue drain as completion.
> 
> Tests cover fake lifecycle (`t_dma_tracker`), FPGA round-trip/reacquire (`t_gof_dma`), and a new FPGA leak suite (`t_gof_staging_leaks`).
>

items.title: Make token-tree `used` pin-derived; fix used-set leak and lost-wakeup hang
items.body:
## Summary

An alternative fix to the token-tree lifecycle bugs Alexey's stress test exposes
(#2862 coalescence, #2863 `used`-set, #2864 hang), stacked on `axch-verify-used`
with the three invariant checks cherry-picked in so it validates against the
strongest workload (100 waves, all asserts on).

**Re-diagnosis of #2864:** it is **not** a stack overflow — reproduced and
captured all-thread backtraces showing a **lost-wakeup deadlock** (test thread on
the wave latch, scheduler worker asleep on an empty queue). It is the *same*
defect as the #2863 `used`-set undercount: a wrongly-cleared `used` ancestor of a
live request makes `compute_forward_args` prune the subtree, the listener never
fires, the pipeline drains, the worker sleeps. (Full write-up:
`for_claude/token-tree-new-approaches.md`.)

## Approach: pin-derived `used`

- `used()` is now an inline accessor derived from a per-node `pins_below` counter,
  not an incrementally-maintained flag. Pins come from (1) client `seq_tip`s and
  (2) pending listeners. This makes the used-set **exact by construction** and
  guarantees a subtree with in-flight work is never pruned — killing the hang.
- Drop `mark_used`/`mark_unused`/`check_usage` and all ad-hoc `used = true` growth
  writes (the source of the leak).
- `seq_tip::set_node` funnels pin/unpin (release on the worker); split seeds the
  intermediate's pins; coalesce transfers them; release follows tombstones.
- #2862: coalesce idle single-child intermediates on release (detected via
  `pins_below == child->pins_below`); relax the invariant for directly-pinned
  single-child nodes (which legitimately cannot coalesce until released).
- `verify_used_set` additionally asserts no pending listener survives at
  quiescence.

## Validation

- `t_token_tree_stress` (100 waves, all three invariants): 20/20 runs green,
  "All tests passed (303 assertions)". ~70x faster than baseline (the slowness was
  used-leak-driven traversal growth).
- `t_token_cache`: pass (74 assertions / 8 cases).
- `t_stream_generate_race`: 2/2 on FPGA.
- `make format`, `make lint` clean.

## Relationship to #2871

Targets the same root cause as Wade's #2871 (which is directionally right);
differs by deriving `used` from a single subtree pin counter (exact, no
boolean-closure recomputation) and pinning in-flight listeners directly.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **High Risk**
> Changes core scheduler token-tree lifecycle, pinning, coalescing, and forward traversal invariants; bugs could strand requests or corrupt eviction/used-set behavior.
> 
> **Overview**
> Replaces the token tree’s incrementally maintained **`used` boolean** with **`used()` derived from `subtree_pins`**, counting client **`seq_tip` holds** and **pending listeners** (pinned on extend, unpinned when notifications fire). **`mark_used` / `mark_unused` / `check_usage`** and ad-hoc `used = true` on reuse/split/create are removed so the live set matches pins by construction and **`compute_forward_args` no longer skips subtrees that still owe in-flight work** (lost-wakeup hang).
> 
> **`seq_tip::set_node`** is the single funnel for tip repoints (pin new, worker release/unpin old); **`release_node`** follows tombstones, unpins, and may **`coalesce_if_unpinned_single_child`**. Coalesce/split transfer pin counts; **`coalesce_nodes`** refuses parents with listeners and merges **`subtree_pins`** onto the survivor. **`verify_tree` / `verify_used_set`** gain listener and deferred-coalesce checks; stress tests bump waves and assert used-set per wave. **`stream_generate`** uses **`unpin_node`** when clearing an eagle speculator without enqueueing release.
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit a3e710673b62bec5bab5d4aad076af7f6c1ff021. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>

items.title: Resolve corrupted work_req assertion in TP2
items.body:
In TP2 or higher, it is possible for a work_req to be reused too soon. When the issue occurs, the following log messages are logged:

```
[error] TRON_ASSERT(other_sp.m_star != -std::numeric_limits<float>::infinity()): Encountered -inf m_star in a valid scratchpad. KV_head 5, to worker 0, from worker 11, batch_job_ix 6
```

Currently, this problem is quiescent with the original heap implementation, but when `TRON_USE_ARENA_ALLOCATOR=1`, the defect is reproduced very quickly in soak tests.

The fix is to make sure the previous work request is finished before reusing to begin a new prepare.
- Add wait_until_work_req_idle()
- Wait for previous launch of a work_req to complete before mutating

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes synchronization on the hot path for hardware matmul/attention scheduling; incorrect ordering could stall or mis-handle in-flight work, but the fix uses an existing atomic guard already set at enqueue and cleared on completion.
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes a **TP2+ race** where plugins reuse the same `wqentry` / `hardware_job` launcher while matmul/attention launches are still asynchronous: the main thread could **fill or prepare** the next job before TX/RX workers finished reading the prior entry, leading to corrupted `work_req` state (especially visible with `TRON_USE_ARENA_ALLOCATOR=1`).
> 
> Adds **`wait_until_work_req_idle`**, which spins on `wqentry::in_flight` with **acquire** loads until the prior job’s completion callback clears it with **release** (set at enqueue, cleared after the job completes). That wait runs at the start of **matmul/attention fill**, **matmul prepare**, and **attention prepare** so fields are not mutated while a launch is still in flight. Documents the protocol in **Note [WQEntry Reuse Race]** and ties the existing enqueue `in_flight` store to that note.
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit ac19c45de1a1e1e19d08a9603d3debe89a0c06af. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>

items.title: Planning layer: iterative walker + HW-attention model state
items.body:
## Planning layer: iterative walker + HW-attention model state

Ports the GoF/shard **planning layer** from `hwattention_sync`: the recursive→iterative
scheduler rewrite (golden-gof-shard descent/ascent) together with the model-side
HW-attention state it drives.

This is a re-slice of the original plan. The walker (`full.hpp`) and the model HW-attention
state (`model.hpp`/`self_attention.hpp`/`common.hpp`) are **one inseparable feature** — the
walker reads model state and `model::forward` consumes what the walker produces (bidirectional),
so neither half compiles without the other. The boundary that *does* hold is **planning layer**
(this PR: scheduler + model headers) vs **execution layer** (next PR: `src/pos` device runtime).

### Inert on `main`
HW attention is **off by default** (`hw_attn_config.hpp`'s `USE_HW_ATTN` gate;
`fwd_hw_attn_enabled()` → false), so `hw_attn_eligible` stays false and every HW-attn block in
the walker is skipped. The only always-on change is the recursive→iterative tree-walk refactor,
which is behavior-preserving. No build-infra change; no CI label needed.

### Commits
1. **Code** — `full.hpp` (walker), `full.cpp`/`generation.cpp` (handle_id propagation),
   `model.hpp`/`self_attention.hpp`/`common.hpp`/`llama.hpp` (HW-attn state, `construct_hw_plan`,
   `prepare`/`launch_hw_attention`), `token_tree.hpp` (drop obsolete PR-9 note).
2. **Docs + tests** — 5 new HW-KV design docs (`attention-scheduling`, `hw-kv-sched`,
   `hw-kv-sched-detailed`, `hw-kv-examples`, `hw-kv-design`) + 2 relocated `golden-*` docs + the
   `doc/images/` figures they reference + `doc/tree-vis/` (Python tooling that generates the
   figures); `t_phase1_integration` and `t_phase2_integration`.

### Reviewing aid
`full.hpp` is the big bite. It interleaves two things in the same functions: (a) the
recursive→iterative conversion (a no-op refactor) and (b) the GoF/shard descent/ascent semantics.
They don't separate cleanly into commits, but reading them as two passes helps.

### Verification
`make build` + `make lint` clean; ported code byte-identical to source. `t_phase1_integration`,
`t_phase2_integration`, `t_scheduler`, `t_token_cache`, `t_generate_2/3`, `t_generate_host_2` pass;

> **Medium Risk**
> Large cross-cutting scheduler/model changes and async GOF DMA when HW is enabled; mitigated by default-off gate and behavior-preserving SW path, but the iterative walker refactor still warrants careful review.
> 
> **Overview**
> This PR lands the **planning layer** for hybrid FPGA/CPU attention: extensive design docs (walker flattening, GOF/shard lifecycle, ranged SW/HW masks, join phase) plus **`doc/tree-vis/`** tooling to generate radix-tree figures for those docs.

KV **`save_k` / `save_v`** now drive **GOF completion** (`save_count` → **`gof_rodeo`**) to populate GOFs and enqueue shard DMA via an optional per-model **`dma_tracker`**. HW attention stays **off unless `USE_HW_ATTN=1`** and eligible devices exist; the paired scheduler walker rewrite (iterative descent/ascent for GoF/shard planning) is described in the PR but is the other half of the same feature boundary.

items.title: Serialize hugepages tests with RESOURCE_LOCK to prevent lock contention

labels.name: Continuous integration
labels.description: Relates to CI

items.body:
The 6 hugepages-labelled tests (t_bf16, t_permutation, t_safetensors,
t_pos_lifecycle, t_heap, t_alloc) share one exclusive flock on
/dev/hugepages/libpos but carry no RESOURCE_LOCK. The host CI job runs
`ctest -LE fpga -j`, so they execute in parallel and collide on that lock:

    INIT: Allocating 16 hugepages from /dev/hugepages/libpos* on numa ALL
    [error] Failed to acquire lock after 8 attempts

This surfaced on #2832 but is a latent race affecting any branch — purely a
function of CI scheduling, not the PR diff.

This adds `RESOURCE_LOCK hugepages_lock` to all 6 tests so ctest serializes
them, mirroring the existing `RESOURCE_LOCK fpga` pattern.

Originally authored by @jwiegley (f90c80934), where it has been stranded
inside the still-open Cachix CI-migration PR #2198; extracted here as a
standalone fix for main. Unblocks #2832.

Note: once this lands, #2198 will conflict on these 6 lines — drop its copy
of f90c80934 on rebase.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> CMake-only test properties; no application code, auth, or data paths affected.
> 
> **Overview**
> Adds **`RESOURCE_LOCK hugepages_lock`** to six tests that allocate from `/dev/hugepages/libpos` so **CTest** serializes them under parallel runs (`ctest -j`), matching the existing **`RESOURCE_LOCK fpga`** pattern.
> 
> **Catch2** tests updated via `add_catch_test`: `t_bf16`, `t_permutation`, `t_safetensors`, `t_pos_lifecycle`. **`t_heap`** and **`t_alloc`** get the same lock on their `set_tests_properties` lines. No production or runtime behavior changes—only test scheduling to avoid flock contention failures in CI.

items.title: h/runtron, perfetto: stream_generate phased-tracing + token-timing instrumentation
items.body:
## Summary

Ports the accumulated `stream_generate` tracing/logging instrumentation from
`hwattention_sync`, plus the matching `tronperf` `--help` text and a
`README.perfetto.md` note. Completely orthogonal to the GoF/shard merge stack —
depends on nothing in it.

## What's in here

- **`TRON_TRACE_FROM_TOKEN=N`** (env-gated phased tracing): with `--trace-gen`,
  defers phase 2 (start tracing) until the total token position (prompt +
  generated) reaches `N`. Default `0`/unset preserves the original behavior
  (trace from prompt-parse completion). Lets long-context captures keep the ring
  buffer on steady state instead of warm-up.
- **`LOG_TOKEN_SELECTION` / `LOG_TOKEN_TIMES`** debug macros — `#ifdef`-guarded,
  commented out by default, inert unless explicitly defined.
- **`perfetto/tronperf`** — `--help` documents `TRON_TRACE_FROM_TOKEN`.
- **`README.perfetto.md`** — user-facing docs for the same var.

## Behavior change (benign — calling out)

Per-token timing source switches from `std::chrono::clock::now()` to
`tron::hardware::system::tsc_in_ns()`. This changes `state::token_start`
(`clock::time_point` → `uint64_t`) and the `report_token` signature; both call
sites are self-contained within this file. Affects **logged timing values only**,
not generation results. `tsc_in_ns()` already exists on `main`
(`h/system/system.hpp`).

## Test plan

## Summary

Wave-2 gatekeeper slice from `hwattention_sync`: token-tree edge state for the
hardware-attention scheduler. Adds the per-edge GoF/shard ownership fields, the
`node_base` shard/gal virtuals, and supporting caches — **all inert on `main`
today** (nothing populates `gals`/`shards` until the walker lands). Also folds in
the #2820 DMA bug fixes and a small scheduler-trace enrichment.

## What's in here

items.title: src/tron + h/pos: GoF/Shard implementation + dma_tracker + pos infra
items.body:
## Summary

Long-pole implementation drop for the GoF/Shard merge from `hwattention_sync`, re-cut from the current source-of-truth tip so that Alexey + CursorBot review feedback already lives in-tree (via #2795, which merged into `hwattention_sync` first). **Supersedes #2695**, which was based on an older `hwattention_sync` snapshot.

Lands `src/tron/gof.cpp` (shard ctor/dtor + `xfer_gof`, `gof::populate`, `k/v_hwcacheblock::xfer`) plus the pos-side
infrastructure it depends on. 23 files, organised in three layers matched to the three commits in this branch:

- **Commit 1 — `h/` infrastructure** (7 files): `h/libpos.hpp`,  `h/pos/config.hpp`, `h/pos/device.hpp`, `h/pos/dma/queue.hpp`, `h/pos/hwattention.hpp`, new `h/pos/dma_tracker.hpp`, and a small `h/tron/gof.hpp` update (`dma_tracker` fwd decl, `POS_PER_PAGE` rename, `backfill_shard` signature). Extends `hw_attn_params` (`pre_attn_scalar`, `hw_layers` as `mask_t<128>` per Alexey's feedback in #2795), introduces `dma_xfer_state`, virtualises
  `xfer`/`xfer_blocking`/`isdone`/`wait` on cacheblocks, and adds the per-model `dma_tracker` (renamed from the original
  `device_dma_tracker` on hwa).
- **Commit 2 — `src/` implementation** (11 files): new `src/tron/gof.cpp` and `src/pos/dma_tracker.cpp`; updates to
  `src/pos/{hwattention,driver,device,dma,dma_queue,fake}.cpp` matching the header changes; 1-line CMake add for `gof.cpp`; `src/pos/CMakeLists.txt` adds `dma_tracker.cpp` to both `pos` and `pos_fake`. Also folds in the DEBUG_BARS sibling fix in `src/pos/vfio.cpp` (same `#ifdef` -> `#if` pattern Bill applied to `DEBUG_INIT` in #2695).
- **Commit 3 — Tests** (5 files): new `t/t_gof_dma.cpp` (FPGA round trip) and host-runnable `t/t_dma_tracker.cpp`; `t/t_dma.cpp` and `t/t_mwaitx.cpp` get structured-binding updates for the new 5-field `dma_xfer_state` returned from `xfer_blocks`; `t/CMakeLists.txt` registers the two new tests.

## Stub note

**`gof::backfill_shard` is intentionally a no-op in this PR** (parameters commented out, `TODO` comment). The full implementation walks the scheduler tree via `node_base::tree_parent` / `tree_height` /
`tree_edge_gals` — APIs added by the separate token-tree edge-state patch (PR 9 in the merge plan). No caller in this PR's scope reaches `backfill_shard` (its only invoker lives in the scheduler reshape that depends on those `node_base` virtuals which don't exist on main yet). The 3-arg declaration in `h/tron/gof.hpp` matches.

## What changed vs #2695

This PR is functionally equivalent to #2695 plus the feedback that landed via #2795 in `hwattention_sync`:

- `find_matched_range` end-of-array `last` bug fix (CursorBot).
- `tok_ix` -> `kv_tok_pos` parameter rename + comment on `fill_attn_job_template` (axch).
- `MIN_TOK_IDX_FOR_HWATTN` doc comment reworded to "0-based token position in its sequence" (axch).
- `hw_attn_params::hw_layers` migrated from `std::vector<bool>` to `tron::mask_t<128>` with the empty-mask semantic corrected so a default-constructed mask means "no HW anywhere" rather than the inverted "all HW" (axch).
- `device_dma_tracker` -> `dma_tracker` (renamed on hwa during the same period; per-model instead of singleton).

## Production-path tweaks (intentional, HW-team confirmed)

This is sidecar work in the sense that no new logic activates on main (nothing here calls `gof.cpp`), with three deliberate
production-path changes carried forward from #2695:

- `default_mm_cmd_fifo_depth` 32 -> 1024 (HW-team-confirmed correct value; 32 was a conservative debug default).
- `DmaQueue` producer mutex + wrap-count tracking — closes a race that was latent on main; makes `find_matched_range` debug dumps actually correct.
- `vhbm_map` virtual HBM mapping + `hbm_north/south_offset += bar4_offset` fix in `src/pos/device.cpp`.

## Debug-flag scrub

- `src/pos/device.cpp` continues to carry the `#define X 0` + `#if X` guards for `DEBUG_INIT` / `DEBUG_RESETS` / `DEBUG_VFIO` introduced by #2695.
- `src/pos/vfio.cpp` `DEBUG_BARS` converted to the same pattern. Previously `#define DEBUG_BARS 0` followed by `#ifdef DEBUG_BARS`, i.e. always-on regardless of value.

## File-level port decisions

Eight `h/` + `src/` files were ported at file level from the source branch rather than merged surgically:

- `h/libpos.hpp` — `hw_attn_params` extension touches struct layout pervasively; piecemeal merge fragile.
- `h/pos/device.hpp` — `wqentry` extensions + `dma_xfer_state` struct + several constants intertwined.
- `h/pos/dma/queue.hpp` — atomic state + move semantics + mutex introduce coupled changes throughout the class.
- `h/pos/hwattention.hpp` — virtualisation of cacheblock xfer API cuts across many methods.
- `h/pos/dma_tracker.hpp` — new file.
- `src/pos/hwattention.cpp`, `src/pos/driver.cpp`, `src/pos/fake.cpp` — implement the file-level-ported headers; ported at file level for symmetry.

`h/pos/config.hpp`, `h/tron/gof.hpp`, and the rest of the `src/pos/*.cpp` are surgical (constants + small interface updates).
`src/tron/CMakeLists.txt`, `src/pos/CMakeLists.txt`, and `t/CMakeLists.txt` are surgical adds only — the AVX compile-flag and `nlohmann_json` drift on `hwattention_sync` is intentionally NOT brought across.

## Test plan

- [x] clang-format-19 --dry-run clean (`make format` no-op)
- [x] no trailing whitespace vs origin/main
- [x] no new `#include <cassert>`
- [x] `make build` succeeds locally (814/814 targets)
- [x] `make t_dma_tracker && ./gen/t_dma_tracker` — 414 assertions
      across 25 test cases pass
- [ ] CI green
- [x] FPGA: `make t_gof_dma && ./gen/t_gof_dma` on a card

```
100% tests passed, 0 tests failed out of 78

Label Time Summary:
fake            = 265.64 sec*proc (35 tests)
fpga            = 347.73 sec*proc (19 tests)
hugepages       =  12.44 sec*proc (6 tests)
main            =   0.46 sec*proc (1 test)
min_slices_2    = 143.94 sec*proc (2 tests)

Total Test time (real) = 669.87 sec

The following tests did not run:
         76 - t_slamtest (Disabled)
```
Originally authored by: Mike Cherba, Wado-posi, Brian Hamon


<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **High Risk**
> Changes core POS DMA serialization, HBM addressing, attention job layout, and shutdown ordering for in-flight KV transfers; includes HW-team-confirmed fifo depth and BAR offset fixes that affect all matmul/KV DMA paths once callers adopt gof.
> 
> **Overview**
> This PR lands the **GoF/Shard** hardware-attention offload path: `src/tron/gof.cpp` (shard HBM alloc/free, `gof::populate`, `shard::xfer_gof`, cacheblock DMA) plus the **pos** headers and drivers it needs, without wiring full scheduler backfill yet.
> 
> **Attention job and model contract** — `hw_attn_params` gains `pre_attn_scalar`, a per-layer **`hw_layers`** bitmap (`mask_t<128>`: unset = SW-only), and documented split between model `kv_head_size` and bitfile **`HW_BAKED_HEAD_SIZE`**. `fill_attn_job_template` now takes per-batch **`kv_tok_pos`**, **`shard_layer_t`** HBM bases, and binds a device; work requests carry **`tok_ix_per_b`**, shards, and **`in_flight`**. The global **`hwkv_rings`** / `save_k_to_hardware` entry points are removed in favor of virtual **`k`/`v_hwcacheblock::xfer`** (and blocking variants) with padded K/V shuffles when head sizes differ.
> 
> **DMA completion** — Transfers return **`dma_xfer_state`** (queue, end descriptor, wrap count, optional readback) instead of descriptor pairs. **`DmaQueue`** tracks ring wraps, serializes multi-descriptor submits with **`producer_mutex`**, and completes via **`check_xfer_complete`**. **`dma_tracker`** is per-model (priority queues per device, `await_layer`, `clear_all_dma_trackers` on **`pos_shutdown`**); **`free_kv_weights`** is added. **`xfer_blocks`** / **`wait_for_xfer_blocks`** gain readback verification and richer timeout dumps.
> 
> **Device / config** — Command FIFO depth default **1024**, **`attn_supported`** from caps, **`vhbm_map`** for KV readback, and HBM BAR offset fixes. KV layout constants move to **`pos/config.hpp`**; tests add **`t_gof_dma`** (FPGA) and **`t_dma_tracker`** (fake).
> 
> **`backfill_shard`** remains an intentional no-op until token-tree **`node_base`** APIs exist; no production caller depends on it in this drop.
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit a081e297b310e8bef78d6b75fd9994b665bd142b. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>

items.title: pos/alloc: instrument HBM allocator with FUSE stats and HBM_ALLOC_SHADOW
items.body:
## Summary

Stacked on #2785. Instruments `tron::hardware::allocator` (the HBM allocator) with FUSE stats and opt-in caller-attribution shadow map, mirroring `pos_heap_v2`'s observability surface for the host DMA heap.

- `/rinzler/stats/devices/<bdf>/allocator/{capacity,free_max,free_total,free_blocks,allocations,deallocations}` — six gauge/counter endpoints per device. Byte stats are whole-device totals (scaled by `FETCHERS_PER_DEVICE` internally).
- `HBM_ALLOC_SHADOW` (compile-time CMake option on the `system` library): per-allocation caller-PC capture at the `alloc_kv_weights` / `alloc_hardware_weights` API boundary plus a `dump_profile()` diagnostic. Symbol resolution via `addr2line` against the rinzler binary.
- Write-triggered `dump_profile_trigger` FUSE control file per device — `echo 1 > .../dump_profile_trigger` fires a snapshot to `$TRON_HBM_PROFILE_PATH`. Always reads as 0.
- OOM error messages in `driver.cpp` now include caller PCs unconditionally (useful even without HBM_ALLOC_SHADOW); SHADOW build also fires `dump_profile("kv_OOM" / "weights_OOM")`.

This is the "extract to main" companion of the same work that exists on `pos_heap_v2`. Commits cherry-picked verbatim from the original development, plus one compatibility commit (`580ad39a1`) that aligns `src/pos/fake.cpp` with the structure used on hwattention_sync (drop the local minimal `struct PosDevice`, use the real one from `pos/device.hpp`, change `fake_devices` to a nullptr-initialized `PosDevice*` array, add empty `devices` global + `pos_list_devices()`) and adds explicit `#include "pos/alloc.hpp"` to `src/rinzler.cpp` / `src/runtron.cpp` so `pos_devices_register_fuse_stats()` is visible without relying on a transitive include path that doesn't exist on main.

Used in the diagnosis of MMLU heap-exhaustion crashes that motivated [STORY-425](https://www.notion.so/positron-ai/356d132d3cfd81f28995f545be1bd260). Related characterization work tracked under [STORY-446](https://www.notion.so/positron-ai/35ed132d3cfd81d48e1ee87bcc26c276) (HBM allocator fragmentation characterization).

## Test plan

- [x] \`make build-test\` clean
- [x] \`make test\` — same parallel-contention pattern as the base branch; all directly-relevant tests pass individually: \`t_heap_v2\`, \`t_tronstats_convention\`, \`t_pos_lifecycle\`, \`t_pos_lifecycle_fake\`, \`t_heap\`, \`t_alloc\`.
- [x] HBM_ALLOC_SHADOW build path: \`cmake --preset native -B gen-shadow -DHBM_ALLOC_SHADOW=ON\` then \`cmake --build gen-shadow --target rinzler -j\` builds clean.
- [x] Used in MMLU diagnostics on \`pos_heap_v2\` — \`dump_profile\` output is well-formed and resolves cleanly via \`addr2line -e gen-shadow/rinzler -f -p <pc>\`.
- [ ] CI passes
- [ ] Reviewer-approved

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes allocator layout behind a compile flag and registers live device pointers in FUSE callbacks; misconfigured `HBM_ALLOC_SHADOW` across TUs would corrupt `PosDevice`, but the PR routes the macro through `system` to prevent that.
> 
> **Overview**
> Adds **observability** to the per-device HBM `tron::hardware::allocator`, parallel to the host `pos_heap_v2` story: fragmentation gauges (`free_total`, `free_blocks`), capacity, and cumulative alloc/dealloc counters, plus optional **caller-PC shadow** when `HBM_ALLOC_SHADOW` is enabled at configure time (declared **PUBLIC on `system`** so `sizeof(allocator)` stays consistent wherever `alloc.hpp` is included).
> 
> **FUSE** exposes `/rinzler/stats/devices/<bdf>/allocator/*` (byte metrics scaled by `FETCHERS_PER_DEVICE`); shadow builds add write `dump_profile_trigger` / read `dump_profile_output`. **`rinzler` / `runtron`** call `pos_devices_register_fuse_stats()` before stats start.
> 
> **Driver** paths `alloc_kv_weights` / `alloc_hardware_weights` always record return addresses for OOM logs; shadow builds also `dump_profile` on failure. A sysfs test confirms **read callbacks** can return strings larger than stored-value limits.
>

items.body:
## Summary

Initial draft/RFC from an investigation into loading `gpt-oss-120b` TP4 on a vatlas4 system.

The vatlas systems are a new bring-up target for this workflow. Please read this as evidence from loading `gpt-oss-120b` onto a vatlas4 system, not as a settled runtime policy. This is not my area of expertise, and I am skeptical of the implementation until someone familiar with generated model loading, `app_pool`, tensor placement, and FPGA weight loading reviews it carefully.

This PR is a single commit against `main`. It intentionally does not include the #2614 in-process weights-cache work or the previously cherry-picked `99c6708f2db8e38fa1932c4c42d89cba72479e44` commit.

## Changes

- Generated expert safetensor loading now calls a C++ helper that visits experts in parallel.
- Per-tensor quantization/load work uses bounded fanout via `TRON_PER_TENSOR_LOAD_WORKERS`, defaulting to 16 workers.
- `set_hardware_weights` is serialized per target `PosDevice`; `alloc_hardware_weights` remains unwrapped because the allocator path already locks.
- Rotated placement shares atomic rotation state across loader threads while preserving thread-local placement contexts.
- Tag-selected model builds pass `--min-support working` so local `support_level: none` overrides cannot emit stale plugin declarations.

## Evidence

Tested candidate:

```text
base:          main
commit:        b556b5527
binary sha256: dd7cb0c14ae73fa642469a7e8e1a644c092af5d7ea3f99e668ae1580f6b7d5ae
```

Live load results on a vatlas4 system:

| Model shape | Result | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `gpt-oss-120b` TP4 | success | 108.359s tensor allocation/load; about 149.4s from config start to ready |
| `gemma-2-9b` TP1, replication 4 | success | slowest instance loaded in 18.247s; slowest add-to-ready about 40.0s |
| `llama-3.3-70b` TP2, replication 2 | failed | both instances segfaulted at dense safetensors token-embedding load, not the expert-parallel path |

The earlier cached-weight baseline for `gpt-oss-120b` TP4 spent 497.782s in the model-load phase, so the current candidate is comfortably under the 10 minute platformd watchdog for that shape.

## Test Plan

Checks run before updating this PR branch:

```text
uv run --with pyyaml python config/test_model_definitions.py: pass, 48 tests
uvx ruff format --check config/test_model_definitions.py: pass
git diff --check: pass
fourmolu on touched Haskell files: pass
clang-format on touched C++ files: pass
targeted t_placer rotated-placement regression: pass
cmake --build gen --target rinzler -j16: pass, 6:13.15
vatlas4 live load, gpt-oss-120b TP4: pass
vatlas4 live load, gemma-2-9b TP1 replication 4: pass
vatlas4 live load, llama-3.3-70b TP2 replication 2: failed as noted above
```

An unbounded local production build saturated the guest and required a reset. The repeatable build command on this system was `cmake --build gen --target rinzler -j16`.

## Review focus

- Is generated expert-load parallelism the right boundary for this optimization?
- Is the per-device `set_hardware_weights` lock sufficient for low-level DMA queue safety?
- Should `TRON_PER_TENSOR_LOAD_WORKERS` default to 16, or should it derive from model shape or hardware metadata?
- Is shared rotated placement state the right representation under parallel expert loading?
- Does the Llama dense safetensors failure expose an existing issue that this PR should avoid touching or explicitly regression-test?

Refs #2776

items.title: move hw_prepare to prep_worker threads per dev

labels.name: Performance
labels.description: Makes things go faster

labels.name: Driver
labels.description: this issue is specific to the driver code

items.body:
Add a prep_worker thread per device and make the main thread call to prepare nonblocking and queue the prepare action to the dev specific thread.

this requires some new synchronization work as prior the serialized sequence served as the synchronization baser but now we need to make that more deliberate.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **High Risk**
> Changes core FPGA driver threading, work-queue ordering, and WQE lifetime; incorrect synchronization could cause hangs, wrong launches, or reuse of in-flight work requests.
> 
> **Overview**
> Moves **`hw_prepare`** off the caller/TX path onto a **per-device PREP thread** with a **`prepwork`** queue, replacing implicit ordering from synchronous prepare with explicit **`wqentry`** gates (`prep_done`, `hw_prepared`) and **mwaitx** waits.

Completion callbacks (or the direct-launch path) set **`prep_done`** so entries can be reused.

> **`prepare_and_launch_direct`:** Optional **`direct_launch`** lets the PREP worker enqueue to **`inwork`** after prepare (used by MoE **`prepare_and_launch_direct`**), reducing cross-FPGA serialization on the main prepare/launch sequence.
> 
> **Ops/tuning:** Startup barrier counts PREP per device; prep threads are **joined** on shutdown. **`--prep-cores`** / **`prep_pin_thread`** (currently aliased to helper cores) and default prep core lists in **`system_optimize`**; minor **`resource-map.yaml`** comments. TX path tweaks: larger **`max_cmd_fifo_depth`**, **`short_timeout_ns`** for slot waits, more **`mwaitx`** in **`tx_wait_for_slots`**, prefetch/trace in **`hw_prepare`**, TX waits for prep before launch.

items.title: proper per-model dma_tracker design, sized by model->n_layers

labels.name: Type: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: Tech Debt
labels.description: This label is used for things that are noticed but not connected enough to be diverted and fixed.

items.body:
Removes the hard-coded `hwkv_max_layers` const used to size dma_tracker queues, and replaces the **singleton** dma_tracker with a **per-model** registry pattern, where trackers are only created/initialized inside the hw-attn-eligible code branch.

## Design Notes

### Storage in state
Use `std::optional<tron::hardware::device_dma_tracker>`, default-empty,
`emplace(cfg.max_layers)` inside the hw-attn-eligible branch. Keeps the
allocation inline on `state` (no heap), skips the cost for models that
never engage HW attention (e.g., the EAGLE draft today), and gives every
push/poll/await site a uniform `dma_tracker->method()` form.

### Lambda capture
`model<>::state` is non-movable (mutexes, latch_arena, etc.), so `this`
is a stable pointer for the state's lifetime. The lambdas at `model.hpp:885-889` become:
```cpp
on_await_dma.push_back([this](size_t l) { dma_tracker->await_layer(l); });
on_forward_poll.push_back([this]() { dma_tracker->poll_completions(); });
```

**Chosen approach: process-global tracker registry.**

Add to `pos/device_dma_tracker.hpp`/`.cpp`:
- A file-static `std::mutex registry_mu` and
  `std::vector<device_dma_tracker*> live_trackers`.
- In `device_dma_tracker::device_dma_tracker(size_t max_layers)`: take
  the lock and `live_trackers.push_back(this)`.
- In `device_dma_tracker::~device_dma_tracker()`: take the lock and
  remove `this` from the vector.
- A free function `tron::hardware::clear_all_dma_trackers()` that locks
  the registry and calls `clear()` on every entry. Idempotent.

Use raw pointers (not weak_ptr) because trackers are owned in-place
inside `std::optional<...>` on `model<>::state` — there's no
`shared_ptr` to weaken from. The lifetime guarantee is: tracker's own
ctor/dtor maintain the registry under the same mutex used by
`clear_all_dma_trackers`, so a tracker can't disappear between "we read
the pointer" and "we call clear()" — the dtor would be blocked behind
the registry lock.

`pos_shutdown` calls `clear_all_dma_trackers()` instead of the old
singleton `clear()`. This restores the singleton-era property that
shards pinned **only** by tracker queues get destroyed while devices
are alive — without it, the per-model design would silently regress,
because the tracker (now a member of `model<>::state`) outlives
`pos_shutdown` and would otherwise drop its `shared_ptr<shard>` refs
late, with `shard::~shard()` calling `free_kv_weights(dev, …)` on a
dangling device.

### Concurrency
Each tracker has its own mutex. Target and draft don't share locks.
The DmaQueue's wrap-count head is shared device state read through
`hwcacheblock::isdone(dev, xfer)`; multiple trackers can call it
concurrently — it's the same code path as today, just with different
priority queues feeding it.

Unit test results (including new `t_device_dma_tracker` test):
```
100% tests passed, 0 tests failed out of 80

Label Time Summary:
fake            = 254.54 sec*proc (34 tests)
fpga            = 695.99 sec*proc (24 tests)
hugepages       =  13.18 sec*proc (6 tests)
main            =   0.47 sec*proc (1 test)
min_slices_2    = 130.20 sec*proc (1 test)

Total Test time (real) = 1006.61 sec

The following tests did not run:
         25 - t_clearhbm (Disabled)
         66 - t_hwattention_replay (Disabled)
         80 - t_slamtest (Disabled)
```

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Touches HW-attention DMA completion bookkeeping and shutdown ordering; mistakes could leave in-flight DMA untracked or free shard/device resources in the wrong order. Changes are localized and include new unit tests to cover sizing, lifecycle, and concurrency.
> 
> **Overview**
> Moves GOF/shard DMA completion tracking from a process-wide singleton (`device_dma_tracker`) to a per-model `dma_tracker` stored on `model<>::state` (via `std::optional`) and constructed only when HW attention is enabled/eligible, removing the hard-coded `hwkv_max_layers` cap.
> 
> Adds a process-global registry of live `dma_tracker` instances so `pos_shutdown` can call `clear_all_dma_trackers()` to drain queues and release shard references before devices are torn down; updates GOF rodeo/backfill paths to attribute DMA completions to the owning model’s tracker.
> 
> Updates build wiring to compile the new implementation and adds a focused `t_dma_tracker` test suite (including negative and concurrency/lifecycle cases) to validate sizing, bounds checks, and shutdown-drain behavior.
>

items.title: Implement pos_heap_v2 for DMA-able memory without fragmentation

labels.name: Performance
labels.description: Makes things go faster

items.body:
The investigation of STORY-425 led to a conclusion that the large number of 8K `hwcacheblock` objects being allocated and released was fragmenting the DMA-able, hugepage-backed memory heap.

A specification for an allocator with separate slabs for each allocation size was developed and reviewed. It is part of the changeset for this PR.

The new allocator is *disabled* by default. To enable it, set the environment variable `TRON_USE_ARENA_ALLOCATOR=1`. 

The python fuzzer, `/tools/rinzler-fuzz.py` is able to reproduce the defect (when you run rinzler without `TRON_USE_ARENA_ALLOCATOR=1`). Note: in order for the memory pressure to trigger cache evictions, you need more than the default 16 `POS_NR_HUGEPAGES`. (I use 32.) Evictions typically begin once the memory exceeds 50% used.


<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **High Risk**
> Replaces core DMA allocation plumbing behind a runtime flag and adds new concurrency/ASAN/shadow-map behavior; mistakes could cause allocator corruption, leaks, or crashes under production load. Also changes DMA-range validation and introduces new FUSE stats registration paths that run at startup.
> 
> **Overview**
> Adds a new DMA hugepage allocator, `pos_heap_v2`, implementing per-size-class arenas backed by a hugepage pool (SMALL sub-slabs vs LARGE hugepages), ASAN poisoning/unpoisoning, optional `HEAP_V2_SHADOW` validation + `dump_profile`, and reserve-draining logic to reduce pool mutex churn.
> 
> Wires allocator selection into `pos_heap_setup()` via `TRON_USE_ARENA_ALLOCATOR` (and build default `TRON_ARENA_ALLOCATOR_DEFAULT_ON`), updates DMA allocation wrappers (`dma_allocate*`, `pos_allocate*`, `heap_start/heap_size`, shutdown/leak checks) to route to the chosen heap, and registers a new `/rinzler/stats/dma_heap/` FUSE stats tree with per-class and pool counters plus dynamic tronstats descriptors.
> 
> Extends the HBM allocator with optional `HBM_ALLOC_SHADOW`, caller-PC attribution, fragmentation-oriented stats (`free_total`, `free_blocks`), OOM profile dumping, and per-device FUSE stats under `/rinzler/stats/devices/<bdf>/allocator/`; also fixes a DMA buffer bounds check to use inclusive heap endpoints and adds new tests/make targets (notably `t_heap_v2` and a disabled contention microbenchmark).
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit ff19045fd05fea80d12eea14029ccad86a8793c7. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>
<!-- /CURSOR_SUMMARY -->




## Performance: pos_heap_v2 vs pos_heap

A microbenchmark (`t/t_alloc_contention.cpp`, gated by `[.perf]`) compares both allocators under concurrent threads doing tight `allocate / touch / deallocate` loops. Three scenarios on andoria-06 (16 hugepages, 500 ms wall clock per scenario):

| Scenario | Threads | Legacy ops/s | v2 ops/s | v2 / legacy |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Single-thread baseline (class 3, 8 KiB) | 1 | 2.84 M | 49.6 M | **17.5×** |
| Same-class contention (all class 3) | 16 | 0.78 M | ~2.7 M | **~3.4×** |
| Multi-class parallelism (classes 3, 5, 8, 10) | 16 | 0.83 M | ~6.3 M | **~7.6×** |

Two structural wins:

1. **Per-op cost is lower even single-threaded.** Free-list pop/push on a per-class slab is cheaper than buddy splinter/coalesce on a global tree.
2. **Per-class mutex parallelizes as designed.** Legacy collapses to a single mutex under any concurrency; v2 scales with the number of distinct classes in flight.

### The pool.mu finding

The original v2 had a hidden bottleneck the microbench surfaced: with one slot in flight per thread, every `alloc + dealloc` cycle locked the global `pool.mu` twice (release the slab on dealloc-when-empty, acquire one on the next allocate). Per-class `arena.mu` parallelism didn't help because the work crossed the arena boundary on every cycle.

The spec anticipated this — `doc/pos_heap_v2.md` § "Open questions" Q1 RESOLVED:

> Empty-current-slab policy: eagerly return. **If churn shows up in profiling, add a global pressure-aware reserve capped to 1–2 slabs total, reclaimed before any OOM.**

This PR lights up that reserve:

- `arena_deallocate` keeps a SMALL-class slab in `partial_head` when its `nr_live` drops to 0 and no other partial slab exists in the arena. The next allocate reuses it without touching `pool.mu`.
- LARGE-class slabs (each pinning a whole 1 GiB hugepage) are not cached.
- `pos_heap_v2::drain_reserves()` walks SMALL arenas and releases cached empties; called automatically by `allocate` on first failure (implements the spec's "reclaimed before any OOM" guarantee).

A few unit tests in `t_heap_v2.cpp` had been stricter than the spec — they pinned the pre-Q1 "always release" implementation detail. They now call `drain_reserves()` before post-drain counter checks. New test `drain on pressure: cached SMALL reserve releases under acquire failure` directly exercises the spec invariant.

### Net result

- Multi-class concurrent throughput: **30× faster than baseline v2, ~120× faster than legacy.**
- Single-thread throughput: **8.4× faster than baseline v2, 17.5× faster than legacy.**
- `t_heap_v2`: 26 cases, 5570 assertions, all passing. `t_pos_lifecycle`: passes under both legacy and `TRON_USE_ARENA_ALLOCATOR=1`.

items.title: fix HW-attn quality: send prefill tokens through SW always, remove them from hw_plan

labels.name: Type: accuracy
labels.description: improves quality of results

items.body:
**Bug.** Silent SW/HW coverage gap during prefill. The scheduler's
`build_edge_ranges` optimistically moves queries from `sw_mask` to `hw_mask`
every time a shard is popped during ascent and emits an `hw_plan_entry` for
them. The model's `construct_hw_plan`, however, refuses to dispatch HW for
any minibatch where `items.size() > 1` (prompt processing — design intent
that prefill stays on SW for now). The mask and the dispatch decision were
inconsistent: the planner gave the queries to HW, HW didn't actually run,
and SW's `apply_page_tok` gate (`sw_required(job_ix)`) then skipped those K
positions because they were no longer marked SW-required.

Result: for every prefill minibatch where the KV-cache extent crossed
`MIN_TOK_IDX_FOR_HWATTN` (128) — i.e., where the scheduler started moving
queries from `sw_mask` to `hw_mask` at shard boundaries — most of the
legitimate causal K positions were attended over by *neither* SW nor HW.
Layer-0 attention output diverged, cascading through the residual + MLP
into every subsequent layer's K/V writes and leaving the KV cache
materially different at decode start. End-to-end this manifested as the
HW-build model producing degraded, qualitatively wrong output (e.g.
14-token non-reasoning replies vs the SW build's 83-token chain-of-thought
on the same prompt).

**Fix.** In `scheduler::full::forward()`, after `compute_forward_args` /
`finalize_ranges` have built `query_mask` and `hw_plan`, reconcile both
with the model's HW-dispatch gate at the fwd level. When
`token_jobs.size() > 1` (prompt processing — same condition the model
uses), fold each range's `hw_mask` back into its `sw_mask` and clear
`hw_plan`. SW then owns every visible (query, K-position) pair; HW
dispatch stays disabled as designed; mask + plan match reality before
either reaches the model.

**Scope.** Single localized change in `h/tron/scheduler/full.hpp` plus
explanatory Note. No API or schema changes. No behavior change for decode
fwds (`token_jobs.size() == 1` → reconciliation skipped → HW continues to
dispatch as before). The model-side `is_prompt_processing` early-return
in `construct_hw_plan` remains as defense-in-depth.

**Verification.** With the fix applied, the HW-build run produces the
same output as the SW-only run on the test prompt. KV-cache snapshot diff
between modes goes from mean-abs K = 0.12–0.59 across layers 1–31 to bit-identical.

This at least pulls our quality up to expectations while we don't support prefill in HW. That is obviously the next feature/support we should be chasing in this HW branch I guess.

---

```
100% tests passed, 0 tests failed out of 79

Label Time Summary:
fake         = 236.54 sec*proc (33 tests)
fpga         = 623.42 sec*proc (24 tests)
hugepages    =  13.16 sec*proc (6 tests)
main         =   0.46 sec*proc (1 test)

Total Test time (real) = 917.01 sec

The following tests did not run:
         25 - t_clearhbm (Disabled)
         65 - t_hwattention_replay (Disabled)
         79 - t_slamtest (Disabled)
```

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Touches core scheduler HW/SW attention partitioning; a mistake could change attention coverage or performance, but the change is narrowly scoped and gated to prefill (`token_jobs.size() > 1`).
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes a prefill-only HW/SW coverage gap by reconciling the scheduler’s ranged masks with the model’s HW-attention dispatch gate: when the forward contains multiple token jobs (prompt processing), all `hw_mask` coverage is folded back into `sw_mask` and `hw_plan` is cleared so work runs end-to-end in software.
> 
> Also updates several Catch2 test tags (e.g., `llama-3.1-*`, `phi-4`, `gemma2`) to remove the leading `.` so these tests are no longer hidden/opt-in.

items.title: h/tron, h/pos: corrections caught during the main-stack code review
items.body:
## Summary

Backports corrections from the hwattention_sync → main merge stack PRs.

### Code-correctness fixes

- **`h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp`**: removed a duplicate `// Returns true if this was the completing save (count reached 2).` comment above `mark_k_complete` (the line appeared twice).

- **`h/pos/hwattention.hpp`** (`xfer_v_entry`): passed literal `0` as the `readback_offset` argument for non-final fetcher transfers in V xfers. The "no readback" sentinel is `no_readback_sentinel = 0xffffffff`; literal `0` would install a readback at offset 0, which is a real (not dead) offset. The matching `v_hwcacheblock::xfer` in `src/pos/hwattention.cpp` already used `no_readback_sentinel`, so this aligns the inline helper with the canonical call site.

- **`h/pos/hwattention.hpp`** (`check_k_range` / `check_v_range`): silently no-op stubs now have a TODO marker so future readers can grep them up. Bodies remain no-ops pending shard-aware bounds tracking.

- **`h/pos/device.hpp`** (`wqentry::in_flight`): comment claimed `hw_prepare` asserts the field is false on entry. `hw_prepare` in `src/pos/worker.cpp` does not actually assert this. Rewrote the comment to describe what the field tracks without claiming a behavior that does not exist.

### Debug-value reverts

- **`h/pos/config.hpp`**: `maxpolls` back to `1e9 / timeout_ns` (~1 second of polling, was 100×); `max_xfer_time_in_ns` back to 100 ms (was 10 s). Both bumps were debug-only and should not have remained on this branch.

- **`src/pos/device.cpp`**: `DEBUG_INIT` flipped from 1 to 0 and the guard switched from `#ifdef DEBUG_INIT` to `#if DEBUG_INIT` so the value actually gates compilation (the macro is always defined). `DEBUG_RESETS` / `DEBUG_VFIO` converted to the same `#define X 0` + `#if X` form for consistency.

### Cleanup

- **`h/pos/device.hpp`**: removed five commented-out `wqentry` fields from the public struct surface.
- **`src/pos/device.cpp`**: removed three `#if 0` / commented blocks (pseudochannel debug print, init register dump, `wcmd/acmd/mdwd` req-id allocations).
- **`src/pos/CMakeLists.txt`**: dropped unused `nlohmann_json` link from both `pos` and `pos_fake`.
- **`src/pos/fake.cpp`**: TODO comment on `fake_devices` null-deref hazard.
- **`src/pos/device_dma_tracker.cpp`**: bounds-check assert on `await_layer`'s `layer` arg, mirroring `push()`.
- **`h/pos/dma/queue.hpp`**: extended move-ctor / move-assignment comments to state the quiescence invariant the relaxed atomic loads rely on.

items.title: h/tron/models/kv_cache: per-token KV completion counters
items.body:
## Summary

Adds per-token, per-layer KV completion tracking to `tron::page`. New atomic
counter `kv_saves_[offset][layer]` (`std::atomic<uint8_t>[page_size][n_layers]`)
records how many of {K, V} have been saved for each (offset, layer); the call
that pushes the count to 2 is the completing save. Comes with the helpers
`mark_k_complete` / `mark_v_complete` (fetch_add(1, acq_rel), return true on
completion), `is_kv_complete` (acquire load >= 2), and `clear_kv_complete_at`
(relaxed reset across all layers, intended to be called when a new token is
assigned to a page offset).

Two new public accessors for direct V-buffer extraction ride along here:
`v_ptr(layer, kv_head, i_page)` on the `TRON_CHUNK_SIZE != 16` path returns
a raw bf16 pointer into the page, and a new
`get_v(layer, kv_head, i_page, bf16*)` overload on the `TRON_CHUNK_SIZE == 16`
path uninterleaves the striped bf16 storage into a contiguous bf16 buffer.
They have nothing to do with the completion counters; they're called later
by `gof::populate` / `backfill_shard` ([PR #2695](https://github.com/positron-ai/tron/pull/2695)).
They land in this PR because removing them would make this file deviate from
hwattention_sync, and #2695 would then have to add them back.

`page`'s move constructor is replaced with an explicit one because
`std::atomic` is not movable; it copies the loaded counter values
element-by-element with relaxed ordering and is only invoked during
single-threaded vector construction. A forward declaration of
`struct node_base;` is also added ahead of the `tron` namespace contents
for use by future callers.

This feature is **inert** until callers wire it in (#2695 onward). No build
without HW attention is affected, and no existing call site changes.

## Test plan

- [x] clang-format-19 --dry-run -Werror clean
- [x] no trailing whitespace vs origin/main
- [x] no new `#include <cassert>`
- [x] `cmake --build gen --target tron` succeeds locally
- [ ] CI green

## Notes for reviewers

The forward declaration `struct node_base;` is unused in this header today;
later code (Future AoF merge PRs) includes this header and references the type. 
Landing it now keeps the per-PR diffs minimal.

Originally authored by: Wado-posi, Brian Hamon

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Introduces new per-token/per-layer atomic counters and a custom move constructor in `tron::page`, which affects concurrency behavior and object movement in a performance-critical KV cache path. Also extends AVX512 `V` access APIs; incorrect use could lead to subtle correctness/perf issues.
> 
> **Overview**
> Adds **per-token, per-layer KV completion tracking** to `tron::page` via a new `kv_saves_[offset][layer]` atomic counter and helper APIs (`mark_k_complete`, `mark_v_complete`, `is_kv_complete`, `clear_kv_complete_at`) intended to let callers trigger work once both K and V are saved.
> 
> Updates `page` move semantics to an explicit move constructor that copies atomic counter values, and extends V-buffer access by adding `v_ptr(...)` on the non-interleaved path and a new AVX512 `get_v(..., bf16*)` overload to uninterleave stored V data into a contiguous bf16 buffer.

items.title: convert wcmd xfers from DMA back to MMIO like main does

labels.name: Performance
labels.description: Makes things go faster

items.body:
This restores our **performance** to parity with the `main` branch for SW-only attention.

It passes all the primary UTs... and now that we have @mcherba's quality fix, t_generate is also passing again:
```
Running t_hwattention... PASS
Running t_hwattention_2... PASS
Running t_attention... PASS
Running t_compute_attention_unit... PASS
Running t_generate... PASS
Running t_generate_2... PASS
Running t_scheduler... PASS
Running t_rinzler_2... PASS
Running t_gof_dma... PASS
Running t_phase1_integration... PASS
Running t_phase2_integration... PASS
Running t_matmul... PASS
```

I also executed multiple combinations of TP1, TP2, TP4, multi-user, long-context, various models including oss-20b and they all behave as expected.

Also, below is Claude's math on why we don't have to worry about FIFO overflow in the `prepare_` path anymore (with fifo-depth of 1024)
```
Legacy alone: mm_in_flight ≤ max_cmds_in_flight = 12, num_wcmds = 1 per matmul → up to 12 wcmds in flight.

  HW-attn alone: mm_in_flight ≤ 1, num_wcmds = 2 × nshards × B. With B=1 (asserted in prepare_hwattn_cmds) and 
nshards ≤ MAX_B = 32 (asserted in fill_attn_job_template), one HW-attn matmul can carry up to 64 wcmds in flight.

  Mixed: HW-attn requires cmds_in_flight == 0 to launch (its mcif_now = 1). But the converse isn't true — once an HW-
attn matmul is in flight, the next legacy at tx_launch sees cmds_in_flight = 1 < 12 and is allowed to queue behind it. So at 
the same moment you can have 1 HW-attn (≤64 wcmds) + 11 legacy (1 each) = up to 75 wcmds in the device FIFO.

  So the real "worst configuration we could ship today" against mm_cmd_fifo_depth = 1024 is ~75. ~13× under that 
generous limit of 1024.

   The conclusion is — overflow is structurally impossible at current caps — the headroom is more than sufficient today, 
but a guard with the proper retire counter is even more clearly worth having since the bound depends on MAX_B and 
max_cmds_in_flight, both of which could move.
```

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Switches weight-command submission from DMA-descriptor transfers to direct MMIO writes in the matmul TX path; this touches low-level device/ring ordering and could affect correctness under load if tail accounting is off.
> 
> **Overview**
> Restores matmul performance by switching weight command (`wcmd`) delivery from DMA descriptor writes back to **inline PCIe MMIO writes** in `hw_prepare()` for both legacy matmuls and HW-attention, removing the previous descriptor-based `wcmd` transfer path.
> 
> Updates command FIFO sizing assumptions by raising `default_mm_cmd_fifo_depth` to `1024`, and adds/asserts tighter invariants around `wcmd_tail`/`wcmd_tail_a` bookkeeping while cleaning up obsolete debug/assert code in the RX/TX worker paths.
>

items.title: skills: ship /github-weekly, source roster from Notion, auto-extend Week
items.body:
## Summary

Three closely-related drift fixes for the team skills:

1. **Add `/github-weekly` as a shared skill.** PR #5 made `/weekly-progress` call `/github-weekly`, but `/github-weekly` was never committed to this repo — it lived only as a personal command on one machine. Anyone other than the original author hits a dangling reference after `./install.sh`.

2. **Source the team roster from Notion.** Replace the hardcoded 9-row roster tables in `/weekly-progress` and `/github-weekly` with a runtime lookup against the [Accelerator Platform Software](https://www.notion.so/positron-ai/Accelerator-Platform-Software-31fd132d3cfd80a1af67de154a08451a) Notion page, with GitHub handles resolved by querying the `aps` GitHub team. One source of truth — the page is what changes when the team changes.

3. **Auto-extend the Stories DB `Week` dropdown.** Adds a step to `/weekly-progress` (Step 0.5) and `/flow-create` (Step 1.5) that ensures the current week's option exists in the Stories DB `Week` select, auto-extending 8 weeks ahead via `notion-update-data-source` if not. Fixes the "Week dropdown only goes to W18" symptom Jesse flagged today; the dropdown self-maintains from now on.

## Why

The check-in flow had three accumulating sources of drift:
- A skill referenced from another skill but not shipped (#1)
- Two hand-maintained rosters that diverged any time the team changed (#2)
- A Notion select that needed manual extension every quarter and silently broke things when forgotten (#3)

This PR collapses each into a single canonical source.

## Changes

- `skills/github-weekly/SKILL.md` (new) — frontmatter follows team-skill convention; roster reads from Notion at run time; output is inline by default with optional file save.
- `skills/weekly-progress/SKILL.md` — Step 0.5 ensures current Week exists; Team Roster section replaced with Notion-page reference.
- `skills/flow-create/SKILL.md` — Step 1.5 ensures current Week exists when the user is setting Week.
- `install.sh` — install the new skill.
- `README.md` — document the new skill.
- (Out of band, not in this diff) the Stories DB `Week` select was extended to W26 (Jun 23) to unblock today's W19 work.

## Test plan

- [ ] `./install.sh` reports four skills installed
- [ ] `/github-weekly` standalone produces an inline 7-day report; team roster reflects the Notion page
- [ ] `/weekly-progress` Step 0.5 is a no-op now that W19 exists; deleting and re-running auto-recreates if removed
- [ ] `/weekly-progress --all` runs end-to-end with the new GitHub Activity section
- [ ] `/flow-create` setting Week on a story works without manual dropdown maintenance

items.title: src/tron: heap-allocate token_cache singleton
items.body:
## Summary

The `token_cache()` singleton is a `static token_cache_t it`, which means it gets destroyed during static destruction. Other globals reference it during their own destruction, leading to use-after-destroy races at process exit.

This PR switches the singleton to `static token_cache_t* it = new ...; return *it;` — intentional leak, defers destruction to OS exit. No behavioral change at runtime; only fixes shutdown.

## Test plan

- [x] clang-format-19 --dry-run clean
- [x] no trailing whitespace vs origin/main
- [x] `cmake --build gen --target t_token_cache` succeeds locally
- [ ] CI green

Originally authored by: Wado-posi

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Low risk: change only affects process-shutdown lifetime semantics by intentionally leaking the singleton; normal runtime behavior should remain unchanged.
> 
> **Overview**
> Prevents exit-time use-after-destruction by changing `token_cache()` from a function-local `static token_cache_t` to a heap-allocated singleton (`static token_cache_t*`), so it is not destroyed during global/static teardown.
> 
> This is an intentional leak to avoid other globals (e.g., scheduler shutdown paths) touching `token_cache` after its destructor would have run.
