items.title: move hw_attn_params away from singleton into model-state

labels.name: Tech Debt
labels.description: This label is used for things that are noticed but not connected enough to be diverted and fixed.

items.body:
Addressing [Story 422](https://www.notion.so/positron-ai/move-hw_attn_params-from-singleton-to-per-scheduler-353d132d3cfd81bcb162cbcc6ac3d242). Address this known band-aid from the GPT-OSS / Ingest support work:
```
### Known band-aid: module-scope `gof_params` and multi-model use

`gof_configure` writes to a single module-scope `gof_params` /
`gof_n_layers`. When two models share state space (notably the
target+draft pair in speculative decoding), back-to-back configures
clobber each other. The smaller model's `gof_configure` was
shrinking `gof_n_layers`, leaving gals created afterward sized too
small for the larger model's forward pass — `fire_gof_rodeo` then
tripped `layer < gal->gofs.size()`.

Current band-aid (`src/tron/gof.cpp::gof_configure`): track the
running max of `gof_n_layers` so subsequent shards/gals stay sized
for the largest configured model. Slight memory waste for the
smaller model, functionally correct as long as both models share
architecture (same `n_layers` template, same head counts, same
HW eligibility pattern).

The proper fix is to move `gof_params`/`gof_n_layers` out of
module scope and into per-model (or per-state) storage so each
model owns its own HW-attn config.
```

UTs pass, runtron combinations execute as expected.

## Summary

- Deleted the module-scope `gof_params` / `gof_n_layers` / `gof_is_configured` (plus `gof_configure` / `gof_configured` / `gof_max_layers` / `gof_hw_params` / `gof_layer_uses_hw` / `gof_reset`) from `gof.cpp` / `gof.hpp`. Removed the running-max band-aid along with them.
- Per-model HW-attn config now lives on `self_attn_state`: existing `hw_attn_cfg` plus new `hw_attn_configured` / `hw_attn_max_layers` flags. `model::state` ctor writes the `hw_layers` mask and validation asserts directly into `hw_attn_cfg`.
- `shard` ctor takes an `hw_attn_params const*` and stores it; `xfer_gof` and `backfill_shard` read from `sh->hw_params` instead of module-scope state.
- Scheduler (`full.hpp`) reads `state.self_attn_state.hw_attn_*` at every prior getter site and threads `&state.self_attn_state.hw_attn_cfg` into the shard ctor and `gof_job::hw_params`. Dropped the `min(n_layers_for_gof, model_t::n_layers)` clamp that only existed to compensate for the running-max band-aid.
- Tests: `gof_guard` rewritten as a local holder of `hw_attn_params` + `max_layers`; shard ctors that need HW pass `&gg.params`. Three test cases that asserted on the deleted module-scope contract were removed and the section numbering updated.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Touches the HW-attention/GOF dispatch and shard allocation plumbing (scheduler ↔ model state ↔ DMA), so mis-threaded params or gating could break HW offload or cause invalid HBM accesses. However, changes are largely a state-ownership refactor with added invariants/asserts and updated tests.
> 
> **Overview**
> Moves HW-attention configuration ownership from `tron::hardware` module-scope GOF globals to per-`model::state` storage, so concurrent models (e.g. target+draft speculative decoding) no longer clobber each other’s `hw_attn_params`/layer counts.
> 
> `shard` now stores a `hw_attn_params` pointer supplied by the scheduler/model state; shard allocation gating, `xfer_gof`, and `backfill_shard` read per-model params instead of singleton GOF state. The scheduler and GOF job wiring switch their enablement checks to `self_attn_state.hw_attn_eligible`/`hw_attn_max_layers`, and the model ctor sets the `hw_layers` mask plus validation asserts.
> 
> Also consolidates HW constants by moving `hw_baked_head_size`/max fetchers/max KV heads out of `pos/config.hpp` into `libpos.hpp` (`HW_BAKED_HEAD_SIZE`, `FETCHERS_PER_DEVICE`, `HW_MAX_KV_HEADS`, `HW_RMEM_WIDTH_ELEMS`) and updates driver/worker/shuffle/test sizing and loops accordingly, deleting tests that depended on the removed GOF singleton API.
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 4911789da40188dbb05bf993d18373bfd5443e15. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>

items.title: Scope GOF mate replication to this edge's flat-array range
items.body:
## Problem

`t_scheduler` and `t_generate_2` were tripping a kv_complete assertion in `fire_gof_rodeo`:

```
TRON_ASSERT(job.gal_ptr->pages[p].kv_complete_fn(layer)):
  GOF rodeo for job 3 but token at pos 2 not kv_complete at layer 0
```

The GOF mate replication loop in `full_scheduler` matched mates by abs position alone, picking the first `token_jobs` entry whose `token_positions` equals `mate_pos`. With branching, two edges can produce gals at the same gof position; the unfiltered match assigned the same `tok_id` to both gals' `gof_jobs` slots, and the later replication overwrote the earlier. `save_k`/`save_v` then incremented the wrong gal's `save_count`, the count hit 8, the rodeo fired, and the gal read its own pages — which the saves had never touched (`kv_saves=0`). Hence the assertion.

Concretely, in the failing run: a gal at `gof_pos=3` belonging to a branch edge (`edge_base=2`, `edge_start_idx=55`) captured `pages[2,3]` from its own `kv_book` (`0x...10b980`/0,1), but the saves for `tok_id=2,3` came from the *root* edge writing to `0x...15bb00`/2,3.

This regression is on `ff35fc684`, not `1224520e7` (mcherba's hwattention sync change).

## Solution

Restrict the replication search to tok_ids in `[edge_start_idx, edge_start_idx + edge.token_count())` so each gal accumulates `save_count` only from its own edge's saves. Mates without an in-edge save target fall through to the existing preload path.

## Test plan

- [x] `gen/t_scheduler` — 4 clean runs (was failing every run pre-fix)
- [x] `gen/t_generate_2` — 2 clean runs
- [x] `make lint`

items.title: resolve minibatch race in GOF firing
items.body:
When running `gen/t_generate_2` at "tp1" (all eight FPGA devices claimed), a `TRON_ASSERT` fires in fire_gof_rodeo (h/tron/models/model.hpp:1597): "GOF rodeo for job 17 but token at pos 348 not kv_complete at layer 0"

The problem is that in TP1, the minibatch size is sometimes not a multiple of 4, which produces a situation where the downstream minibatch can fire the GOF before the upstream has finished writing the mates' K/V.

The fix provided here:

Replace the firing-token-only predicate `(pos+1)%gof_tokens==0 && k_completing` with a per-GOF, per-layer atomic `save_count` on `tron::hardware::gof`. Every `save_k`/`save_v` on a GOF participant — firing token or non-firing mate — does `fetch_add(1, acq_rel)`; the increment that reaches `2*gof_tokens` (8) fires `gof_rodeo`. At gal construction, mates already kv_complete from prior forwards (or non-query mates without saves coming) are pre-loaded by 2. The scheduler also replicates the firing slot's `gof_jobs[]` entry into each non-firing query mate's job_id, so any mate's save can fire and `gof_rodeo_impl` produces identical work via shared `gal_ptr`/`tok_position`/`shards_getting_gofs`.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Touches concurrency-critical paths (GOF dispatch and DMA descriptor submission) using atomics and new locking; correctness depends on memory ordering and avoiding deadlocks/contention under high parallelism.
> 
> **Overview**
> Prevents premature `gof_rodeo` dispatch when GOF mates complete across different minibatches by adding a per-(GOF, layer) atomic `gof::save_count` and firing only when all 8 K/V saves have been observed.
> 
> Updates `save_k`/`save_v` to increment the counter (with `acq_rel` ordering), and updates the scheduler to replicate `gof_jobs` entries to non-firing query mates and pre-load counts for mates already `kv_complete` from prior forwards.
> 
> Hardens DMA queue usage by adding `DmaQueue::producer_mutex` and locking the multi-descriptor `write_next_descriptor` + `update_tail` sequence in `xfer_blocks` to avoid concurrent ring corruption/crashes.
>

items.title: pos/driver support for head_size 64, selective layers in HW, plus UT coverage
items.body:
these changes pass all UTs that currently run in our branch plus the new one... they also pass the various tron permutations: TPx, x-Users, short/long context etc.

## Summary

Lays the device/driver-side groundwork for two gpt-oss-20b features on the existing head_size=128 bitfile: (a) running with model `head_size = 64` by zero-padding to the bitfile geometry, and (b) declaring per-layer HW eligibility so sliding-window layers can be skipped on the HW path. No model-side dispatch changes yet — the `head_size == 128` gate at `model.hpp:830` is still in place; this PR makes the lower stack ready for it.

## Changes

**`hw_head_size` constant + model/HW head_size split**
- New `hw_head_size = 128` in `h/pos/config.hpp` documents the bitfile-baked per-head W-MEM/HBM cell count.
- `hw_attn_params` (`h/libpos.hpp`) gains `hw_head_size` alongside the existing `kv_head_size` (model). HW-side stride/layout/DMA paths now read `hw_head_size`; model-side reads continue to use `kv_head_size`. `ah_kvh_size` is still programmed from `kv_head_size`, so the systolic working width tracks the model.
- `xfer_k_packed_entry` / `xfer_v_entry` (`h/pos/hwattention.hpp`, `src/pos/hwattention.cpp`) take both head sizes; HBM stride math switches to `hw_head_size`.
- New padded-shuffle helpers `shuffle_k_head_padded` / `shuffle_v_entry_padded` write a model-`head_size` source into a `hw_head_size` destination layout, leaving the upper cells as zero pad. K cacheblock `set_position` overloads accept both sizes.

**Per-layer HW eligibility**
- `hw_attn_params` gains `std::vector<bool> hw_layers` plus a `layer_uses_hw(layer)` accessor (empty ⇒ all layers HW-eligible, preserving legacy behavior).
- New `gof_configure(hw_attn_params const&, max_layers)` overload threads the field through; the legacy 5-arg overload is unchanged. New module-scope getter `tron::hardware::gof_layer_uses_hw(layer)`.
- Per-shard HBM allocation in `src/tron/gof.cpp` now skips SW-only layers — `kv_shard_layers[l] = {0, 0, 0}` when `!layer_uses_hw(l)`, and the dtor short-circuits on `layer_alloc_bytes == 0`.
- `model.hpp` populates `hw_layers` from `plugin.layers[l].attention.sliding_window_size != illegal_sliding_window` at gof-configure time. Still gated on `head_size == 128` for now.

**Tests (`t/t_hwattention_2.cpp`, FPGA)**
- Coverage for `hw_attn_params` / `gof_configure` / shard alloc gating / padded shuffle helpers.
- HBM round-trip test at `head_size = 64`.
- `unity_matrix_head_size_64` — full FSM flow (Q + K/V → DMA → HW attention → result readback) at `head_size = 64`, validating that result buffers stay at the bitfile-sized 160 entries with valid data in the first half and `sume`/`smax` at the bitfile offsets.
- `unity_matrix_head_size_64_multi_layer` — same flow over layers `{0, 2, 4, 7}` to exercise the per-layer HW mask at the device boundary.

```
Running t_rinzler_2... PASS

Running t_phase1_integration... PASS
Running t_phase2_integration... PASS
Running t_matmul... PASS
```

> **Medium Risk**
> Touches HW-attention KV shuffle/DMA sizing and shard HBM allocation paths; mistakes could corrupt HBM layout or mis-handle layer skipping, though changes are guarded by asserts and extensive new FPGA tests.
> 
> **Overview**
> Enables running HW attention with a **model `kv_head_size` smaller than the deployed bitfile’s per-head layout** by introducing a separate `hw_head_size` (via new `hw_baked_head_size` constant) and updating cacheblock shuffles and HBM DMA sizing/stride math to use the HW geometry while padding unwritten cells with zeros.

items.title: Perfetto enhancements and additional events
items.body:
I've had very limited luck leveraging the 'fill_policy' (and other related settings) in runtron.cfg for 'limiting' the perfetto captures. We actually already have/support phase(1), phase(2) and phase(3)  perfetto phases in the code. "phase 2" is 'generation only' (omits the prefill/prompt-parsing activity). So if we pass --gen as an argument in the tronperf script, that's what you get.

I'm currently using an environment-var strategy where I can set TRON_TRACE_FROM_TOKEN to whatever (e.g. 4096), and if that var is defined, the code will delay the phase(2) invocation until we land on that token, then it will capture to the end of the run.

Caveat: To keep things simple for now, it does require the use of --gen flag when calling tronperf . So prompt tokens are skipped in the traces altogether *if* this env-var is supplied.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Medium risk because it changes when phased Perfetto tracing starts (including potentially never starting) and adjusts latch/phase synchronization to avoid deadlocks; incorrect thresholds could lead to missing or unexpected traces but shouldn’t affect model outputs.
> 
> **Overview**
> Adds a new phased-tracing control `TRON_TRACE_FROM_TOKEN` that delays Perfetto *phase 2* (generation tracing) until the combined prompt+generated token position reaches a configurable threshold, allowing tail-only captures for long runs.
> 
> Hardens the tracing lifecycle in `runtron` by making the start latch one-shot (avoids UB from double `count_down`) and by releasing the start latch on any `phase >= 2` to prevent deadlock when phase 2 is skipped.
> 
> Improves trace usability by extending `perfetto/runtron.cfg` duration for long-context runs and adding/adjusting additional `TRACE_EVENT`s in the scheduler and GOF shard backfill path; docs and `perfetto/tronperf` help text are updated to describe the new env var.
>

items.title: t_clearhbm: direct-mode poison + ECC verify (STORY-385)
items.body:
## Summary

Reworks `t_clearhbm`'s poison mode to write through the WIM/RIM (9/8) window instead of the Bypass (8/8) window, so the source buffer bytes land in both data and ECC regions of each 576-byte `strip`. Adds a verify mode that confirms the write survived via an identity-matmul readback.

Background from STORY-397: the Bypass DMA used by the previous poison path auto-fills scale bytes to bf16(1.0), regardless of source bytes. That mechanistically explains why every previous attempt to reproduce the post-power-cycle defect through `TRON_POISON_BITS` has failed — the ECC bits the defect depends on weren't reachable through that path.

Two commits:
- **`t_clearhbm: call get_devices()`** (latent bug fix, separable): `ClearHbmListener` was calling `pos_startup()` directly, which populates the device mask but skips the per-device TX/RX worker spawn. Any matmul or `set_hardware_weights` call would then spin forever on `tx_worker_ready`. Switch to `get_devices()` which does both atomically. Prerequisite for any matmul work in this test.
- **`t_clearhbm: add direct-mode poison and ECC verify (STORY-385)`**: main change.

## Behavior

Three modes, gated by env vars (composable):
- `TRON_POISON_BITS=0` (default): zeroize mode, unchanged from before.
- `TRON_POISON_BITS=X` nonzero: direct-mode poison. Writes `uint16(X)` repeated into every byte of the full weight-region HBM (all 32 fetchers × 1.125 GiB = 36 GiB per device, parallel across 8 devices), via 9/8 DMA.
- `TRON_VERIFY_ECC=1`: after the poison pass, run identity-matmul readback and assert every output cell equals `bf16(X) × dequant[low_nibble_of_low_byte(X)]`.

## Scope note

Per project convention, `t_clearhbm` remains a unit test (`DISABLED TRUE` in `t/CMakeLists.txt`, opt-in via `./gen/t_clearhbm`). Promotion to a first-class tool is out of scope.

## Empirical results (STORY-385 FoM)

Ran `TRON_POISON_BITS=0x7fc0 ./gen/t_clearhbm` followed by runtron on andoria-06 (`llama-3.1-8b-instruct-fast`, prompt-length 380, length 644):

| Condition                       | Post-power-cycle defect   | Direct-mode poison `0x7fc0`                          |
| ---                             | ---                       | ---                                                  |
| 1st runtron after setup         | Fails with attention NaN  | Fails with attention NaN (`m_star != -inf` assert)   |
| 2nd runtron (no intervening op) | Succeeds (state self-clears) | Fails again (poison persistent)                   |
| Runtron after zeroize           | Succeeds                  | Succeeds                                             |

**Capability achieved:** direct-mode poison puts a card into an attention-NaN state on demand and that state is clearable via the existing zeroize path. Zero false negatives on `TRON_POISON_BITS=0x4444 TRON_VERIFY_ECC=1` (all 32,768 output cells match expected `0x4544` bit-for-bit).

**Signature difference from real power-cycle defect:** our direct-mode poison is strictly more aggressive than the real defect. It persists across runtron invocations because it overwrites the full 9/8 window (36 GiB per device), where the real defect is almost certainly a much smaller ECC-state anomaly that any single runtron op overwrites in passing. Because zeroize clears both, the two states share a family of "ECC/scale bytes in a bad configuration."

**Value delivered by this PR:**
- Eliminates the power-cycle step from the FPGA team's debug cycle. Any candidate fix has to survive a test that triggers attention NaN via poison and clears via zeroize, without the multi-minute overhead of a physical power cycle.
- Narrows the defect's home to something the 9/8 window can address and zeroize's bypass-path bf16(1.0) auto-fill can clear.
- Provides a stronger stress test than the power-cycle defect itself (since our poison is wider).

**Finding a surgical pattern** that reproduces the power-cycle defect's exact fail-once-pass-after signature is a separate empirical search — tracked under STORY-395 (bisection modes) for systematic exploration, or via FPGA-team input on what the post-power-cycle ECC state actually is.

## Coverage caveat

The `reserved[16]` field of each `strip` (32 bytes of ECC region per strip) is not consumed by the systolic, so verify cannot observe it. If the defect pattern turns out to live specifically in `reserved`, a different observation mechanism is needed — out of scope for this PR, tracked under STORY-396.

## Test plan

- [x] `make gen/t_clearhbm` — clean build
- [x] `make format` — no changes needed
- [x] `make lint` — clean
- [x] `make build-test` — clean (verified by author)
- [x] Zeroize sanity (no env vars): all 9 Catch2 assertions pass on andoria-06
- [x] `TRON_POISON_BITS=0x4444 TRON_VERIFY_ECC=1`: all 32,768 output cells (4096 × 8) match expected `0x4544` bit-for-bit, exit 0
- [x] `TRON_POISON_BITS=0x7fc0` followed by runtron: **runtron fails with attention NaN on first invocation**, confirming direct-mode poison successfully induces a defective attention state
- [x] Zeroize + runtron: **runtron succeeds post-zeroize**, confirming recovery

## Related stories

- [STORY-385](https://www.notion.so/positron-ai/344d132d3cfd8167abe6d39d5940edc3) (this PR)
- [STORY-397](https://www.notion.so/positron-ai/346d132d3cfd8185af3ff95f3692454c) (done): characterization that showed bypass DMA auto-fills ECC to bf16(1.0)
- [STORY-396](https://www.notion.so/positron-ai/346d132d3cfd813ebe14c5e57d6caa06) (deferred): reading un-written HBM requires FPGA-team input
- STORY-395 (blocked on 385): bisection modes for FPGA team debugging

items.title: reduce compiler noise under nix
items.body:
## Background
The nix configuration file `flake.nix` specifies the toolchain and all dependencies for the tron repository. A key benefit of nix is the ability to encapsulate the development environment (tools, dependencies) into that configuration file, so that changes in tools/dependencies can be developed and released as regular PRs. Although the CI runners are set up to begin leveraging this capability, at present, they continue to rely on Ansible scripts to maintain consistent native configurations on those hosts.

I have begun to use the `nix develop` shell on my development host, to understand its impact to our work flow; and to identify and fix any problems that we will encounter once the CI hosts switch over.

An early finding was that the Clang v19.1.7 compiler that is available in the `nix develop` shell includes a cc-wrapper that is configured with a slightly more-hardened set of compiler options than the native Ubuntu-packaged clang v19.1.7 compiler. Due to these subtle changes, code that had previously built without warnings is now emitting warnings. This PR resolves the ones that I have been seeing on the `hwattention_sync` branch. 

## Changes
- Check function return values causing warnings in `huge.cpp`, `t_rinzler_{1,2}.cpp`
- Fix `src/pos/dma_queue.cpp`: unnamed `lock_guard` — lock was never actually held

This PR features the same single-commit patch as in PR #2357, rebased onto `hwattention_sync`. That other PR has been closed.

## Test plan
- [ ] CI green on this branch
- [x] Spot-check `t_rinzler_1` / `t_rinzler_2` run clean



<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Medium risk because it changes synchronization in `DmaQueue::acquire` (potentially affecting queue allocation behavior under concurrency) and touches low-level hugepage file truncation handling, though changes are small and mainly add error checking/logging.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Reduces new clang/nix build warnings and fixes a real locking bug.** `DmaQueue::acquire` now stores the `std::lock_guard` in a named variable so the mutex is actually held while selecting/initializing a queue.
> 
> In `huge.cpp`, `ftruncate` failures are now checked and logged instead of ignored, and the Rinzler integration tests explicitly ignore the return value of `system("id > /dev/null")` to silence warnings.
>

items.title: fix unit tests, fix formatting
items.body:
PR summary                                                                                                                                                 
                                                                                                                                                             
  Fix xfer_gof: DMAing unpopulated gof! assertion in backfill path
                                                                                                                                                             
  - **Bug**: When a new shard is created mid-descent, backfill_shard walks up ancestor edges to DMA prior GOFs into it. Some of those GOFs were never populated, because in an earlier pass their owning gof_rodeo_impl bailed on  shards_getting_gofs.empty() — no live shard covered the position at the moment KV completed, so populate() was skipped. Later shard creation hit the g.populated assert in shard::xfer_gof (src/tron/gof.cpp:95).                            
  - **Fix 1** — lazy populate in backfill_shard (src/tron/gof.cpp): Before calling xfer_gof, if the gof isn't populated, call populate() using the target shard's device and the gal's retained page_info. The gal's page lambdas remain valid (pages backing live queries can't be evicted), so the data is still reachable.
  - **Fix 2** — skip re-populate in gof_rodeo_impl (h/tron/models/model.hpp): Rodeo now guards on !g->populated before calling populate(). This lets backfill and rodeo run in either order — whichever sees the gof first populates it; the other just DMAs. Without this guard, the gof-already-populated assert in populate() fires when backfill wins the race.
  - **Tests:** All four previously-failing tests pass — t_generate, t_generate_3, t_scheduler, t_rinzler_2
  - **Follow-up (out of scope)**: Disabled "Simple Gemma 2 test" in t/t_rinzler_2.cpp with a TODO. It exposes a pre-existing bug: gof_configure is process-global; when rinzler loads llama-3.2-3b (head_size=128, 28 layers, HW-eligible) alongside gemma-2-9b (head_size=256, 42 layers, not HW-eligible),  gemma inherits the stale gof_configured()==true and gof_max_layers()==28, and its 42-layer forward tries to fire rodeo at layer 28. Needs a per-scheduler HW-attention flag instead of the global check; not introduced by this PR, just unmasked once the backfill abort is gone.                                   

**UT test results:**

```
Label Time Summary:

         36 - t_generate_host_2 (Disabled)

         71 - t_slamtest (Disabled)
```

runtron tests all pass as well, with both 3b and 8b models, up to 4096 tokens

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Touches HW attention KV-cache population/DMA ordering and adds conditional behavior that can affect correctness under concurrency; failures would surface as missing/incorrect KV transfers or attention results.
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes a HW-attention backfill crash where `backfill_shard` could attempt to DMA a `gof` that was never populated (because `gof_rodeo_impl` had no live shards at creation time). `backfill_shard` now *lazily populates* any unpopulated GOFs before calling `xfer_gof`, and `gof_rodeo_impl` now skips `populate()` if another path already did it.
> 
> Standardizes HW-path KV-head sizing by introducing `hw_max_kv_heads` in `pos/config.hpp` and using it for HW-attn eligibility checks and `gof::populate` bounds/stack arrays. Includes minor formatting-only changes and disables the Gemma2 integration test (marked `[.gemma2]`) due to a known 32-layer HW-attn limitation.

> **Medium Risk**
> Touches hardware-attention planning, DMA/shard scheduling, and cross-thread synchronization; regressions could cause incorrect attention outputs or intermittent races under load.
> 
> **Overview**
> Restores correct HW-attention execution by fixing several HW/SW boundary and synchronization issues that previously caused HW to not activate, race on Q (RoPE), or read invalid addresses.

> **Medium Risk**
> Touches HW-attention KV offload scheduling and GOF→shard DMA dispatch, so mistakes could cause incorrect attention results or DMA hangs; changes are localized but alter core runtime logic and lifecycle resets.
> 
> **Overview**
> Refactors GOF handling to introduce `gal` (GOF-for-all-layers) as the authoritative per-edge store, shifting `gof_job` from owning per-layer GOFs to pointing at an edge-owned `gal` and wiring shard recipients during scheduler ascent; `gof::populate()` now takes external `page_info` and DMA dispatch filters shards by token-range overlap.

> Updates `full_scheduler` to (1) create shards via *trailing boundary* logic (including optional leaf “trailing” shards), (2) propagate eligible shards up the tree and stop pushing shard chains when DMA/offload eligibility fails, and (3) gate HW attention planning to single-token (non-prompt) minibatches. Adds `hwkv_min_gofs_for_offload` and `shard::count_complete_gofs()` to enforce minimum-context/partial-shard rules.
> 
> Improves DMA bookkeeping by adding `device_dma_tracker::clear()` (called from `pos_shutdown()` and `gof_reset()`), plus bounds assertions in `push()`. Removes unused `shard::zero_v_hbm()`, adjusts backfill to replay `gal` GOFs, and updates/expands integration tests to cover the new gal/shard logic.

Implements golden-gof-shard.md design by merging the best parts of two independent implementations:

- gal struct as authoritative GOF store (unique_ptr on edges)
- Query-driven gal creation with page_info on gal
- Trailing boundary shard creation logic
- Ascent-based shards_getting_gofs propagation
- Shard push filtering with hwkv_min_gofs_for_offload threshold
- DMA tracker clear() + bounds assertions
- Comprehensive phase1-5 integration tests

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Touches scheduler traversal, HW KV offload eligibility, and DMA/backfill paths, so mistakes could cause incorrect attention results or missed offloads. Changes are contained to the GOF/shard offload pipeline and are covered by expanded integration tests.
> 
> **Overview**
> Replaces per-edge GOF storage with an edge-owned **authoritative `gal` (GOF-for-all-layers) repository**, where each `gof_job` points at a `gal` holding the shared `page_info` and per-layer GOFs.
> 
> Updates the scheduler’s GOF/shard pipeline to be *query-driven*: `gal` objects are created only when a query token completes a GOF, shards needing the GOF are determined on ascent (`shards_getting_gofs`), and `gof_rodeo_impl` now DMAs only to shards whose token ranges cover the GOF position.
> 
> Reworks shard management by creating shards via **trailing-boundary logic**, adding shard offload eligibility filtering (including `hwkv_min_gofs_for_offload` and partial-shard handling), and making DMA tracking more robust via `device_dma_tracker::clear()`, bounds assertions, and reset/shutdown cleanup. Integration tests are extended to cover the new phases and edge cases.

items.title: Clear HBM using raw xfer_blocks per fetcher
items.body:
A new unit test, `t_clearhbm` is added (disabled for normal CI runs) which uses an approach developed by @Wado-posi to clear the HBM. This runs on all the devices in the instance in parallel for speed.

On Atlas, with the FPGAs running bitfile `archer_128col_nan_reg.rbf` , I ran the following command after cycling power on the box, waiting for the system to come back online, confirming that platformd finished successfully, then ran the following commands:

```
cd ~/code/tron
export TRON_LOG_LEVEL=info
SYSTEM_CONFIG="--instance 0,2" gen/t_clearhbm & SYSTEM_CONFIG="--instance 1,2" gen/t_clearhbm & wait
```
Within 15 seconds the command completed successfully. Afterwards, any runtron command run on any card would produce meaningful output (no gibberish, no NaNs). An example of such a command is:

items.title: fix t_matmul divide-by-zero?
items.body:
See the comments in the code-delta... when I asked Claude to explain why this works fine on main branch, but breaks here... this was its explanation:
```
● On main: wqentry has no default member initializers at all — it's a plain aggregate. new wqentry does default-initialization, which
  for POD-like types leaves members indeterminate. So bytes_per_res_block is whatever junk was in the heap.                             
                                                                                                                                        
  On this branch: you added shards{} and nshards = 0 (default member initializers). In C++, once a struct has any default member        
  initializer, new wqentry triggers value-initialization of the whole object, which zero-initializes all members without explicit       
  initializers — including bytes_per_res_block = 0.                                                                                     
                                                        
  So on main, bytes_per_res_block is uninitialized heap garbage, which is almost never exactly 0, so the divide "works" (by accident).  
  On this branch, it's reliably 0, so it crashes every time. The bug has always existed — it was just latent on main.
```

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes the call ordering for streamed matmul results so `prepare_matmul` must run before `hardware_job::stream_results()`, affecting launch/streaming sequencing. Low code churn, but touches hardware job preparation/launch flow and could impact streaming behavior if callers rely on the old (incorrect) order.
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes a crash in streamed matmul result handling by **making `prepare_matmul` a required prerequisite** for `hardware_job::stream_results()` (which uses `bytes_per_res_block` and could previously divide by zero).
> 
> Adds explicit documentation (`Note [Stream Results Prepare Dependency]`) and updates the emulation `device_matmul` streaming path to call `prepare_matmul` before setting up streams, then launch normally.
>

items.title: TSX-based mwait
items.body:
Implement mwaitx using TSX/RTM with tpause.

mwaitx is triggered by touches to the trigger's cache line.

RTM transactions cause the transaction to abort when the trigger's cache line is touched.  The transaction entails a tpause in a rdtsc() loop.  The processor resumes as if the tpause didn't happen.  Meaning immediate wake up.   This is effectively just how mwaitx works. Clever!   (not my idea).

items.title: Enable pos_shutdown in test listener with DMA cleanup

labels.name: Driver
labels.description: this issue is specific to the driver code

labels.name: Intel
labels.description: Run CI build on Intel runner (delphi)

items.body:
## Why this change exists

`pos_shutdown()` was commented out in test listeners across the codebase with the note: *"Crashes and burns due to unfreed allocations."* This caused:

1. **Every test binary leaked hugepages and DMA allocations** (tracked in #1733)
2. **Intermittent segfaults in `t_dma`** during process exit (#1535, #2400) — all 3 test cases pass, then the process segfaults during teardown because the kernel tears down VFIO BAR mappings while static destructors still reference them

The root cause: `PosDevice::init()` allocates DMA buffers and queues, but nothing freed them. `pos_shutdown()` was disabled because calling it triggered heap asserts on the outstanding allocations.

## What changed

### DMA cleanup infrastructure
| Change | Why |
|--------|-----|
| `PosDevice::destroy()` | Matching free for `init()`. Without it, heap assert fires on shutdown. |
| `hwkv_rings` destructor | Frees 128 cache block DMA allocations. |
| `delete device` + `devices.clear()` in `pos_shutdown` | Without this, device objects leak and restart appends duplicates. |
| Zero-init pointer members in `PosDevice` | `destroy()` null-checks before freeing; uninitialized pointers cause garbage `dma_deallocate`. |
| `pos_heap_active_allocations()` | DMA allocation counter (real heap + fake-mode). Enables leak detection in test listeners. |

### t_dma segfault fix (#1535, #2400)
| Change | Why |
|--------|-----|
| Enable `pos_shutdown()` in `TestDmaListener` | Without it, process exit races VFIO BAR teardown against static destructors → segfault. |
| Release DmaQueues in transfer test | Test acquired TX/RX queues per device but never called `release()`. |
| Baseline allocation tracking | Record `pos_heap_active_allocations()` after `pos_startup()`, warn only if tests leak above that baseline. The 288 device-init allocations (64 device.cpp + 64 consumed_head + 32 ring buffers + 128 hwkv_rings) are expected. |

### Restart lifecycle hardening
| Change | Why |
|--------|-----|
| `pos_startup()` idempotency guard | Prevents duplicate device scan if called twice without shutdown. |
| `vfio_groups = nullptr` after delete | Prevents double-free on second shutdown. |
| `get_group_fd` EBUSY retry | IOMMU teardown is async; rapid restart cycles hit EBUSY on group reopen. |

### Test + review feedback
| Change | Why |
|--------|-----|
| `t_pos_restart` (3 FPGA cases) | Restart produces same device count, idempotency, double-shutdown. |
| `t_pos_lifecycle_fake` (6 cases) | Shutdown with outstanding allocs, allocation tracking, reinit. |
| `INFO()` diagnostic in lifecycle test | Per mcherba review — surfaces allocation count on failure. |

## What this does NOT change

Production behavior is unaffected. `pos_shutdown()` was already called at process exit in Rinzler. The only behavioral change is in test infrastructure — listeners now clean up instead of leaking.

### Superseded by main (resolved during merge)
- Inline group init in `vfio_device_init` → main serialized into `vfio_init_groups()` (better race fix)
- `host_initialized` double-call guard → landed independently on main

## Test results

- `make test-host`: 53/53 passed (cloud-atlas-873f)
- `t_dma`: 5/5 clean runs on 8 FPGAs, zero segfaults, zero leak warnings, clean `pos_shutdown()`
- `make format && make lint`: clean

## Test plan

- [x] `make build-test && make test-host` — 53/53 pass
- [x] `t_dma` — 5 consecutive runs, clean shutdown, no segfault
- [ ] `t_pos_restart` (FPGA CI) — restart lifecycle regression tests
- [ ] `t_pos_lifecycle` (FPGA CI) — existing lifecycle tests
- [ ] Full CI matrix (AMD + Intel runners)

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Touches shutdown paths for FPGA/VFIO + DMA heap lifecycles; bugs here can cause use-after-free, leaks, or restart flakiness, but changes are narrowly scoped to cleanup and tests.
> 
> **Overview**
> Ensures `pos_shutdown()` actually frees **DMA-backed** resources instead of leaking hugepages/VFIO state, enabling safe teardown in tests and repeated `pos_startup()` cycles.
> 
> Adds `PosDevice::destroy()` and defensive member initialization to release DMA queues/buffers and disable mailbox/tracer write targets before BAR/IOMMU teardown; also gives `hwkv_rings` a destructor to free its ring allocations. Introduces `pos_heap_available()`/`pos_heap_active_allocations()` (real + fake) and improves heap shutdown diagnostics.
> 
> Hardens restart behavior by making `pos_startup()` idempotent, fully deleting/clearing device/global state in `pos_shutdown()`, nulling `vfio_groups` after free, and retrying VFIO group open on `EBUSY`. Updates test listeners to warn on DMA leaks, re-enables shutdown in `t_dma` (and releases per-test queues), and adds new lifecycle/restart regression tests (`t_pos_restart`, expanded `t_pos_lifecycle_fake`).
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 5e2d19d3626d679ccd20003a4de46f4975a15373. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>

items.title: Replace hwkv allocation with shard
items.body:
This is a follow-on PR to PR 2089, which adds GOFs and shards. Here we remove the allocation mechanism that was introduced on hwattention_sync as part of the AOF development effort, which supported only a single model and concurrent user, and switches to the GOF/shard infrastructure.

This is a work in progress, and depends upon PR 2089 merging to hwattention_sync first.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **High Risk**
> High risk because it changes how HW attention finds and manages KV cache HBM addresses (moving from a global singleton to per-shard allocations) and touches scheduler/GOF save/flush paths that can affect correctness and performance across layers.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Moves HW KV cache ownership from the global `hwkv_rings` singleton to per-`shard` HBM allocations.** Shards now allocate and free per-layer K/V HBM regions (`alloc_kv_weights` + new `free_kv_weights`) and GOF DMA paths write into these shard bases.
>

items.title: GOF/shard DMA implementation with TRON_SHARD_TEST=1
items.body:
Introduces a new path for writing K/V data into FPGA HBM using group-of-four (GOF) blocks. Tokens are accumulated into 4-token `gof_buffers`, promoted to immutable `completed_gofs` on completion (zero-copy swap), then DMA'd to HBM. The new path is gated by `TRON_SHARD_TEST` env var — when unset, the existing `save_k/v_to_hardware` path is used.



<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **High Risk**
> High risk because it adds a new hardware KV DMA write path (including completion polling and blocking gates) and extends token-tree edge split/coalesce logic to preserve new GOF/shard state, which could impact correctness and concurrency in scheduling and HW attention dispatch.
> 
> **Overview**
> Adds a new *experimental* GOF/shard-based KV-to-HBM transfer pipeline gated by `TRON_SHARD_TEST`, accumulating K/V into 4-token `gof_buffer`s, promoting them to immutable `completed_gof`s (zero-copy swap), and DMAing them to device HBM with optional partial-token flushes before GOF completion.
> 
> Introduces `device_dma_tracker` to track per-device in-flight DMA and expose `poll_completions()` plus `await_layer()`; wires this into the scheduler/model loop via new observer hooks (`on_forward_poll`, `on_await_dma`, `on_flush_partial`) and extends `save_k`/`save_v` observers to receive a `node_base*` hint.
> 
> Extends the token-tree (`node_base` + `parent_edge`) to store shards, completed GOFs, embryonic GOFs, and per-session `handle_id`, and updates edge split/coalesce paths to correctly move/merge this new state; adds an FPGA test (`t_gof_dma`) and build plumbing for the new sources.
>

items.title: fix wqentry->result_size calculation
items.body:
`fill_attn_job_template()` was treating `wqentry->result_size` as a count of bytes rather than count of scalars. Based on use in the code, it seems clear that field is intended to be a count of bf16 **elements**, not bytes:

1. `launch_work_req` does a memset using `work_req->result_size * sizeof(bf16)` as the size if PREFILL_WITH_NANS is enabled
2. in `prepare_cmd_words' pad_bytes is multiplying by POS_DATA_SIZE to get bytes: `pad_bytes = res_bytes_per_act - (workreq->result_size * POS_DATA_SIZE);`
3. it seems wqentry->result_size is intended to match 'hw_results_size', which is a scalar and is calculated in self_attention.hpp as `static constexpr size_t hw_result_size = n_heads * (head_size + 32);` (no multiply by sizeof(bf16)
4. `hardware_job::stream_results()` treats that 'result_size' as an element count when calculating blocks
5. inside of `fill_hardware_matmul_job_template()` for matmul operations, that field is assigned directly from the 'result_size' passed in: `work_req->result_size = result_size;` (no sizeof(bf16) multiplcation)... and that 'result_size' comes from the models which always calculate as "n_heads * head_size"
6. the documentation for this field in device.hpp is pretty clear that it intends a scalar count ('fpga columns')

The main challenge I had was trying to validate this change in a definitive way... runtron runs didn't seem to produce any differing behavior before/after the change. I did run t_hwdriver, t_hwattention, t_attention, t_compute_attention_unit and t_matmul after the change and they all pass.

items.title: Add observer hooks for save_k/save_v in model::state
items.body:
In preparation for hw-kv-token-tree changes, which will intercept the calls to `save_v` and `save_k` independently, I'm introducing two Observer-pattern hook points: `on_save_k` and `on_save_v`. The parameters being used for calling this hook point will be unchanged, and will be identical to those currently taken by `save_k_to_hardware` and `save_v_to_hardware`.

Registering callbacks must be done before any prompting or generation with a model, to avoid concurrency issues. Here, the registration happens in the model::state constructor, which is guaranteed to be completed before a scheduler can use the model. 

There is one behavioral change. Page write is reordered before observer notification. With this change, the planned GOF readiness observer can find page data already written when it fires. This will not cause any additional latency for the code on the hwattention_sync branch, because both the DMA block and page write calls are blocking. Reversing the order won't affect the total per-token timing.

Implementing these hook points in this way will avoid (as much as possible) merge conflicts between `hamon-hktt-dma` (where hw-kv-token-tree DMA changes are being developed) and `hwattention_sync`. 

Additionally, `make format` identified a number of minor formatting fixes in device.hpp and t_hwattention.cpp 


<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes the KV-save call path and ordering around page writes vs DMA notification, which can affect correctness/timing for hardware attention and any future observers; concurrency expectations depend on observers being registered before inference starts.
> 
> **Overview**
> Introduces **observer-style hook points** in `model::state` (`on_save_k` and `on_save_v`) to allow multiple callbacks to be invoked when KV data is saved, while registering the existing `tron::hardware::save_k_to_hardware` / `save_v_to_hardware` as the default observers.
> 
> Updates `save_k`/`save_v` to **write KV data into the page first**, then collect per-head pointers and notify all registered observers instead of calling the hardware save functions directly. Also includes minor `self_attention.hpp` formatting/comment tweaks (debug macro comment style and line wrapping) with no functional change.
